title: Ensure tab completion works with installed brew package
description: Verify and ensure that shell tab completion works correctly when dogcat is installed via Homebrew (brew). This includes testing that completions are properly registered and functional for the dcat CLI.

title: Add worktree field to Issue data model
description: Add an optional worktree field to the Issue dataclass in models.py to track which git worktree an issue belongs to. This would allow assigning and filtering issues by worktree when multiple worktrees share the same .dogcats directory.

title: Set up dcat web command with FastAPI + Jinja2 + Tailwind skeleton
description: Create the dcat web subcommand (feature-gated behind DCAT_FEATURE_WEB). Set up FastAPI app with Jinja2 templating and Tailwind CSS via CDN. Bind to 127.0.0.1:8000 by default. Add FastAPI and Jinja2 as optional dependencies. Create base template with Tailwind CDN link, navigation layout, and project name header.
acceptance:
- dcat web starts a FastAPI server on 127.0.0.1:8000
- Feature-gated: requires DCAT_FEATURE_WEB=1
- Base HTML template with Tailwind CDN and nav layout
- / redirects to /issues
- --port and --host flags supported
notes: Mobile-first responsive design. Use Tailwind responsive utilities (sm/md/lg breakpoints). Primarily tested on mobile viewports.

title: Issue list view
description: Read-only issue list page showing all issues in a filterable table. Reuse storage.py to load issues. Support filtering by status, type, priority, and labels via query params. Show columns: ID, title, type, status, priority, labels, updated_at.
acceptance:
- /issues route renders a list of all issues
- Filters for status, type, priority, labels
- Sortable by priority and updated_at
- Links to issue detail view
notes: Mobile-friendly layout: stack filters vertically on small screens, compact table or card-based list on mobile.

title: Kanban board view
description: Read-only kanban board showing issues as cards grouped by status columns (Open, In Progress, In Review, Blocked, Deferred). Each card shows issue ID, title, type badge, and priority indicator. Cards link to issue detail view.
acceptance:
- /kanban route renders a kanban board
- Columns for each active status
- Issue cards with key info
- Cards link to detail view
- Responsive layout with horizontal scroll if needed
notes: Mobile-friendly kanban: consider vertical column stacking or horizontal swipe on small screens.

title: Issue detail view
description: Read-only detail page for a single issue. Shows all fields: title, description, status, priority, type, labels, owner, acceptance criteria, design notes, notes, comments, dependencies (blocks/blocked-by), parent/children, external ref, timestamps. Render markdown in description and notes fields.
acceptance:
- /issues/{issue_id} route renders full issue details
- All issue fields displayed
- Dependencies shown with links to related issues
- Parent/children shown with links
- Comments listed chronologically
- Markdown rendered in text fields
notes: Mobile-friendly detail layout: single-column, readable on small screens.

title: Dependency graph visualization
description: Visual dependency graph showing issue relationships. Consider using a JS graph library (e.g., D3, dagre, mermaid) to render blocks/blocked-by and parent/child relationships.

title: History/timeline view

title: Dashboard/summary stats view

title: File-watching event stream library
description: Internal library that watches issues.jsonl for changes and emits events. Uses watchdog for filesystem monitoring. Exposes a Python API (not CLI) that consumers (web UI, future CLI command) can import. Lives in src/dogcat/stream/ or similar.

title: Read-write support for Web UI
description: Add write capabilities to the Web UI: create issues, update fields, change status, close issues, add comments. Requires CSRF protection and form validation. Reuse storage.py write methods.

title: Multi-project support in Web UI
description: Support loading .dogcats/ folders from multiple repositories simultaneously. Add a project switcher in the nav. Single web server instance serves all configured projects. Configuration for project paths (CLI args or config file).

title: Wire live updates into Web UI via SSE
description: Add SSE endpoint to the web server that uses the internal file-watching stream library (dogcat-3tuf) to push issue change events to the browser. Add JS client-side listener to auto-refresh views without polling. Should import the library directly, not shell out to a CLI command.

title: Web UI test infrastructure and tests
description: Set up test infrastructure for the web UI using httpx AsyncClient as the FastAPI test client. Write tests for all routes: /, /issues, /issues/{id}, /kanban. Test filtering, sorting, error handling (missing issues, invalid filters). Test template rendering produces expected HTML structure. Add to the existing pytest suite.

- Route tests for all endpoints
- Filter and sort parameter tests
- Error case tests (404 for missing issues, bad params)

Designed for desktop and mobile, with a mobile-first approach — primarily tested on mobile. Initial version is read-only. Future phases: read-write support, multi-project support, live updates.

description: Add a helper function that detects how dogcat was installed by checking executable path for Homebrew markers (/Cellar/, HOMEBREW_PREFIX), virtualenv (sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix), etc. Used to give contextual install instructions in error messages.

title: Show (minimal) in version output when web deps missing
description: Update dcat --version to check if web dependencies (fastapi, uvicorn, jinja2) are importable. If not, append '(minimal)' to the version string. e.g. 'dogcat 0.11.3 (minimal)' vs 'dogcat 0.11.3'.

title: Improve dcat web error message with install-method-aware instructions
description: Update the ImportError handler in _cmd_web.py to use the install method detection. Show 'brew install dogcat' for Homebrew minimal users, 'pip install dogcat[web]' for pip users, etc.

title: Create dogcat-minimal Homebrew formula
description: Add dogcat-minimal.rb to homebrew-tap. Identical to dogcat.rb but post-install does 'pip install dogcat' instead of 'pip install dogcat[web]'. Same wheel, fewer dependencies.

title: Update dogcat Homebrew formula to current version
description: The Homebrew formula is pinned to v0.10.0 but the project is at v0.11.2. Update dogcat.rb to the latest release.

title: Add optional per-record checksums to JSONL storage
description:
JSONL records in src/dogcat/storage.py have no embedded CRC or hash. A bit-flip or partial write producing valid-but-incorrect JSON is undetectable. dcat doctor can catch structural issues but not data corruption.

Consider adding an optional record-level checksum (e.g., CRC32 trailer) for a stricter validation mode. This would allow detecting corrupted-but-valid JSON records that currently pass parsing without error.

Files: src/dogcat/storage.py

title: Add Windows/non-POSIX fallback for file locking
description:
fcntl.flock() is used directly in storage.py, inbox.py, and event_log.py with no platform detection or fallback. On Windows, the import fails with ModuleNotFoundError.

Fix: Add platform detection with msvcrt.locking() fallback, or document POSIX-only requirement explicitly.

Files: src/dogcat/storage.py:6,230, src/dogcat/inbox.py:5, src/dogcat/event_log.py:5

title: Consider command registry pattern for CLI modules
description:
Each _cmd_*.py module in src/dogcat/cli/ independently imports storage, config, IDGenerator, models. No middleware layer or command registry pattern. Tab completion is manually registered per option in _completions.py. Scales poorly past ~50 commands.

Consider a command registry or plugin pattern if growth continues.

Files: src/dogcat/cli/

title: Reduce compaction latency for large JSONL files
description: Compaction rewrites the entire file under lock (storage.py:39-42). At 10MB+ this could block for hundreds of ms. Consider incremental compaction or background compaction with a write-ahead append buffer.
notes: Deferred 2026-04-26: P3 with no concrete trigger — no benchmark in hand, no user-reported pause. Project explicitly avoids complexity ('no daemon, just JSONL'). Revisit when someone hits a measurable pause; first step would be a benchmark + raised threshold tunable, not WAL/background compaction.

title: Formalize benchmark suite for scale testing
description: No visible benchmarks for >500 issues, large JSONL files, or concurrent access patterns. Formalize benchmark.py into a just benchmark target with known-scale scenarios (1K, 5K, 10K issues).

title: Add retention/rotation policy for event log
description: The event log (event_log.py) is append-only with no TTL, sampling, or rotation strategy. For long-lived projects it grows without bound and can exceed the main JSONL file size. Consider configurable retention (e.g. keep 90 days), periodic compaction, or sampling for older events. Flagged by 2/6 communities in code review.

title: Add dcat recover command to reconstruct state from event log
description: If issues.jsonl corrupts outside of git, there's no recovery path. The event log is append-only and theoretically contains enough data to reconstruct issue state. Add a dcat recover --from-events command. Currently recovery relies entirely on git history. Flagged by 2/6 communities in code review.

title: Allow compaction on non-default branches to prevent file bloat
description: Auto-compaction (storage.py:426) only runs on the default branch. Heavy feature-branch workflows accumulate stale records and the JSONL file grows until merged to main. Consider an optional manual compaction flag or a less restrictive branch heuristic.

title: Add dcat hook install/uninstall/list commands for Claude Code hooks
description:
Add CLI commands to manage Claude Code hooks in .claude/settings.local.json.

## Commands

### dcat hook install <name> [options]
Installs a named hook into .claude/settings.local.json. Creates the file or merges into existing structure. Idempotent — skips with a message if already present.

Available hooks:
- sessionStart: SessionStart event, matcher 'startup|resume|clear', runs 'dcat prime'. With --opinionated flag, runs 'dcat prime --opinionated' instead.
- preCompact: PreCompact event, matcher '' (all), runs 'dcat prime --replay'.

### dcat hook uninstall <name>
Removes the named hook from .claude/settings.local.json. Cleans up empty hooks/event arrays after removal.

### dcat hook list
Shows installed hooks from .claude/settings.local.json. Also shows hooks from .claude/settings.json marked as '(shared)'.

## Edge cases
- No .claude/settings.local.json exists → create it
- File exists but no hooks key → add it
- Hook already installed → no-op with message
- Uninstall hook that isn't installed → no-op with message

## Tab completions
Add autocompletion callbacks for hook names (sessionStart, preCompact) on install and uninstall subcommands, per project conventions.
acceptance:
- [ ] dcat hook install sessionStart adds SessionStart hook to .claude/settings.local.json
- [ ] dcat hook install sessionStart --opinionated uses 'dcat prime --opinionated'
- [ ] dcat hook install preCompact adds PreCompact hook
- [ ] Installs are idempotent
- [ ] dcat hook uninstall removes hooks and cleans up empty structures
- [ ] dcat hook list shows installed hooks (local and shared)
- [ ] Tab completions for hook names on install/uninstall
- [ ] Tests for all commands

title: TUI design sweep follow-up
description: Follow-up work from a /sweep design review across src/dogcat/tui/ and the color/symbol tables in src/dogcat/constants.py. Reviewers: audit, critique, harden, polish, clarify, layout, colorize. ~190 raw findings distilled into 10 Red / 24 Yellow / 10 Green action points; this epic groups them into focused implementation issues. Excludes work already tracked under dogcat-271v (panel compose / _do_update structural refactor).

title: TUI bindings: p priority blocks text input, D force-delete bypass
description: Two binding bugs surfaced by the sweep. (1) detail_panel.py:181: Binding('p', 'pick_parent', 'Parent', priority=True) — priority=True intercepts before focused widgets, so the letter 'p' likely cannot be typed in any text Input/TextArea on the panel while editing. Drop priority=True or guard via check_action against focused-input state. (2) dashboard.py:98: Binding('D', 'force_delete_issue', 'Delete!', show=False) bypasses the confirmation modal entirely; one Shift away from confirmed 'd', hidden from footer. Either remove the binding, gate behind an explicit feature flag, or surface in footer with explicit no-confirm copy. 4 reviewers flagged D; 1 reviewer flagged p (verified).
closed_reason: Dropped priority=True from p binding; removed D force-delete bypass binding, action, and tests

title: TUI data-loss guards on refresh and resize during inline edit
description: Two paths silently destroy unsaved inline edits. (1) dashboard.py:532-546 action_refresh reloads storage and rebuilds the panel even when the inline detail panel is mid-edit; no _is_panel_editing check. (2) dashboard.py:177-188 watch__split_mode -> _clear_detail_panel runs unconditionally on shrink-below-threshold and wipes the editing panel. Both should guard via _is_panel_editing() (already exists at dashboard.py:409-418), similar to editor.py:131-136 which guards action_go_back. Options: block the action with a notify, prompt to save/discard, or preserve the buffer until next show.
closed_reason: Guarded action_refresh + on_resize via _is_panel_editing; reapply split mode on save/cancel

title: TUI form safety: title/desc length, narrow save exceptions, escape Rich markup
description: Three small but real safety gaps. (1) detail_panel.py:667-670 title validation only checks empty/whitespace; MAX_TITLE_LEN=500 from constants.py is not enforced. detail_panel.py:678 description has no MAX_DESC_LEN=50_000 cap. Pasting huge text triggers the generic 'Save failed' path. (2) detail_panel.py:729-730 and :803-804 use bare 'except Exception' which masks programmer errors (AttributeError, KeyError) as user-facing notify toasts. Narrow to (ValueError, RuntimeError, OSError) like dashboard.py:520. (3) dashboard.py:66-67 ConfirmDeleteScreen interpolates issue id/title into Rich markup string; a title containing [red]...[/red] would render styled. Use markup=False or escape.
closed_reason: Pre-validate title/desc length; narrow exceptions to (ValueError, RuntimeError, OSError); escape markup in ConfirmDeleteScreen

title: TUI ConfirmDeleteScreen overhaul: safe-default focus, responsive width, y/n shortcuts, cascade copy
description: ConfirmDeleteScreen has multiple polish/safety issues flagged by 5 reviewers. dashboard.py:27-82. (1) on_mount focuses #yes-btn (variant=error, destructive); reflexive Enter after 'd' deletes — switch to focusing #no-btn. (2) Fixed width: 50 overflows narrow terminals and truncates long titles; switch to width: 90%; max-width: 80 like ParentPickerScreen. (3) No Binding('y'...) / Binding('n'...) for the keyboard idiom — only Tab+Enter works. (4) Dialog body shows only id and title; doesn't surface cascade (orphaned children, unlinked deps) or recoverability (tombstone vs hard delete). Surface destructive consequences. (5) Yes/No button labels could be 'Delete'/'Cancel' for verb-first clarity.
closed_reason: Safe-default focus on Cancel; verb-first labels; y/n shortcuts; recoverability hint; responsive width with min-width: 36

title: TUI color system overhaul: palette overlap, glyph fallback, theme variables, in_review symbol
description: Color was the strongest cross-reviewer consensus (colorize/audit/harden/critique/polish all flagged it). Concrete items: (1) constants.py:65-91 — PRIORITY_COLORS, TYPE_COLORS, STATUS_COLORS overlap heavily: bright_red codes priority=0 + type=bug + status=blocked; bright_black codes priority=4 + type=chore + status=draft + status=deferred; white codes priority=2 + type=task + status=closed (the defaults!); yellow codes priority=1 + the [manual] badge. Re-allocate so each axis gets its own hue family. (2) shared.py:108-117 priority [N] and type [task] are differentiated by color only — no glyph fallback like STATUS_SYMBOLS. Add redundant signal so color-blind users and monochrome terminals don't lose hierarchy. (3) constants.py:208 STATUS_SYMBOLS['in_review'] = '?' — the only ASCII glyph in an otherwise Unicode set; reads as TODO. Pick a real glyph (candidates: ◔ ⊙ ◉ ❖). (4) shared.py:114, 116, dashboard.py:273, detail_panel.py:128 hardcode 'cyan'/'yellow'/'dim' which bypass Textual theme variables (/-muted/) used elsewhere; theme overrides won't apply. (5) shared.py:97-106 dependency-blocked override repaints non-blocked issues to look identical to status=blocked — distinguish (e.g. ■ vs ▣). (6) bright_yellow (in_review, question) and bright_magenta (epic) illegible on light terminals.

title: TUI dependency reconcile: atomicity and actionable error messages
description: detail_panel.py:613-663 _save_dependencies — each add_dependency / remove_dependency call is independently try/except'd inside four separate loops. If add #2 fails (cycle, missing target), adds #1 and removals already committed remain in storage; the user sees one toast per failure (potentially N stacked) and the dep graph is half-applied. Also the message format 'Dependency error: <stringified ValueError>' is opaque for cycles. Fix: pre-validate the entire diff before committing any change, then commit atomically (or roll back on first failure). Translate raw ValueError to actionable text e.g. 'Cycle detected: A -> B -> A'.
closed_reason: Atomic reconcile via _compute_dep_plan: pre-validates entire dep diff (resolve + would_create_cycle) before any storage write; surfaces all errors in single toast

title: TUI empty-state messaging across pickers, filters, and dashboard
description: 5 reviewers flagged silent empty states. Touch points: (1) picker.py:60-67 search filter with no matches shows blank list, no 'No matches' hint. (2) picker.py:105-110 pick_issue() returns None silently when there are zero issues — caller can't distinguish cancel from empty. (3) dashboard.py:323-332 same blank-on-no-match in dashboard search. (4) detail_panel.py:106-132 ParentPickerScreen with no eligible parents shows empty list and a Clear Parent button only — no explanation. (5) dashboard.py:151-168 first-run with zero issues shows empty OptionList with no 'no issues yet — press n' hint. (6) dashboard.py:159, 225 right-pane placeholder is plain unstyled Static. Add teaching empty states that explain navigation/next action.

title: TUI notify wording, severity rubric, and markup policy
description: Notify calls drift in tense, severity, and markup support. dashboard.py:461 'No issue selected' (warning), :466 'Issue X not found' (error), :519 'Deleted X' (no severity), :521 'Delete failed: ...' (error), :546 'Refreshed' (no severity); detail_panel.py:513 'Press [b]e[/b] to enter edit mode' (markup=True — only place using Rich markup), :669 'Title cannot be empty' (error), :796 'No changes to save' (no severity, but also auto-dismisses the form), :635/:643/:655/:663 'Dependency error: ...', :730 'Create failed: ...', :804 'Save failed: ...'. Settle on: one error format ('<verb> failed: <reason>'), one severity rubric (warning vs error vs info), markup always-on or always-off. Also reconsider 'No changes to save' which currently dismisses the form — surprising.

title: TUI stale-data re-validation after refresh and broken-parent detection
description: Two stale-data leaks. (1) dashboard.py:190-213 _show_issue_in_panel calls _storage.get(full_id) and silently returns if the issue was deleted by another process; user keeps seeing the old detail panel. After refresh (dashboard.py:539-544) the highlighted issue may have been removed externally — _get_selected_issue_id returns the now-missing ID and _show_issue_in_panel silently no-ops. Add a 'this issue no longer exists' notice. (2) detail_panel.py:380-386, 517-521 the parent button stores parent ID as a string label; if the parent issue was deleted externally, the button retains the stale ID and saving writes back a broken parent reference. _get_parent_options excludes tombstones, but the *currently selected* parent is never revalidated. Flag broken parent on load.
closed_reason: Detect tombstoned issues on refresh + panel re-show; reparent orphans to root in _load_issues; broken-parent button shows '<id> (deleted)' in bold red, suffix stripped on save

title: TUI split-pane discoverability and resize hysteresis
description: Two related issues with the split-pane mode. (1) constants.py:28-29 + dashboard.py:170-175 — SPLIT_PANE_MIN_COLS=200 and SPLIT_PANE_MIN_ROWS=40 silently toggle the right detail pane. Below threshold the user has no indication that a wider terminal would unlock the inline panel. The 40-row threshold is unusually tall — many laptops sit at rows<40. Add a hint Static below threshold ('Resize wider for split view') and/or a manual toggle binding. (2) Threshold has no hysteresis — dragging across exactly 200 cols toggles split mode on every resize tick, which mounts/unmounts the IssueDetailPanel and re-fetches storage each time. Add a deadband: split-on at 200, split-off at 195.

title: TUI CSS de-duplication and SHARED_CSS expansion
description: Multiple CSS blocks duplicate selectors. (1) editor.py:37-62 IssueEditorScreen.CSS and detail_panel.py:184-225 IssueDetailPanel.DEFAULT_CSS both declare #editor-form, #title-input, #title-bar Button, #description-input, .detail-section-body — drift hazard when one is updated. (2) ConfirmDeleteScreen and ParentPickerScreen each roll their own modal CSS with different units (fixed 50 vs 90% / max 120 vs fixed 24); SHARED_CSS does not own a modal/dialog pattern. (3) picker.py CSS and dashboard.py CSS use different rhythms for the same conceptual element (search input + option list). Consolidate into SHARED_CSS, define a modal pattern, scope panel-specific rules with IssueDetailPanel selectors as already done at detail_panel.py:184-224.

title: TUI spacing scale, vertical rhythm, and modal sizing rationalization
description: Spacing values are ad-hoc across the TCSS. Documented scale is 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 but actual values mix 12, 16, 20, 24, 40, 50, 80, 120 with no shared tokens. Three concerns: (1) Vertical rhythm is monotonous — every section uses margin: 1 (shared.py:16-78); no hierarchy expressed through spacing. (2) Modal heights inconsistent: ConfirmDeleteScreen width: 50 fixed (dashboard.py:39-44), ParentPickerScreen height: 24 fixed with max-height: 80% (detail_panel.py:60-65), SHARED_CSS row max-heights of 5 are likely never reached (shared.py:37-72) and may be dead. (3) Split-pane proportion has dead zone: dashboard.py:122-126 width: 40%; max-width: 80 — at 200 cols, 40% = 80 already pinned, so 40% rule never has effect across most of its range. Define an explicit size token set and apply consistently.

title: TUI escape semantics and footer binding consistency
description: Five different escape behaviours across screens, plus mixed binding labels for the same conceptual action. picker.py:25 escape -> 'Cancel'. detail_panel.py:49 ParentPickerScreen escape -> 'Cancel' (dismiss_picker). editor.py:32 IssueEditorScreen escape -> 'Back', priority=True, but action_go_back at editor.py:131-136 silently no-ops while editing. dashboard.py:93 DogcatTUI escape -> 'Quit', blocked by check_action while panel is editing (silent no-op). detail_panel.py IssueDetailPanel — no escape binding at all; only way to cancel inline edits is mouse-click Cancel. Footer label voice fragments: 'Quit' / 'Back' / 'Cancel'. Settle on one rule (escape = cancel/back) and one footer vocabulary.

title: TUI form layout: button placement, title-bar squeeze, dependency fields, edit-mode indicator
description: Form-layout issues clustered together. (1) detail_panel.py:317-327 Save/Cancel buttons live in the title bar. With description + 3 collapsibles + view-mode sections, user must scroll back up to commit; the actual happy path is Ctrl+S in the footer. Move buttons below the form, or hide them and rely on footer key hints. (2) shared.py:16-30 + detail_panel.py:317-327 title bar packs id-display(min-width 12) + title-input(1fr) + Cancel + Save, no responsive treatment. At 40-col split-pane left, title input gets ~9 cells. Cap id-display, hide buttons below threshold, or wrap. (3) detail_panel.py:387-404 depends-on / blocks fields are disabled Inputs visually identical to enabled inputs, with prefix-as-value ('blocked by: a, b') vs placeholder-as-status ('no blockers') — three style mismatches in one row. Render as Static or beef up disabled styling. (4) detail_panel.py:570-593 enter_edit doesn't add a visual indicator inside the panel itself; only the app title flips. Add an in-panel banner/border/badge. (5) detail_panel.py:380-386 parent button shows bare full_id; rich label captured by picker is discarded. Store the rich label and render it on the button.

title: TUI list label density and tree rendering
description: Issue list rows feel templated and break down in deep trees. (1) shared.py:108-117 make_issue_label produces 3-5 colored bracket fragments per row ([priority] [type] [labels] [manual]) with the title as the only neutral content; chrome dominates. Inverts 60-30-10 weight rule. Mute secondary metadata or right-align it. Inconsistent boldness: status and priority bold, type regular weight (no rationale). (2) dashboard.py:260-276 _build_tree uses 2 * depth spaces for indentation with no glyphs (├─ └─ │) and no depth cap — long titles walk off-screen at depth 4+ on narrow terminals. Use real tree glyphs and consider truncation/ellipsis. (3) shared.py:24-30 #id-display is muted via -muted in title bar despite the ID being the primary identifier users reference. Re-evaluate hierarchy.

title: TUI minor cleanups: dead params, double-indent, app title format, misc
description: Bundle of small isolated fixes. (1) detail_panel.py:235, 244 + editor.py:72/81/185/193 — existing_ids parameter is plumbed through three layers but never consulted in _do_create; either wire up client-side dup-ID validation or drop the param. (2) detail_panel.py:459, 464, 473, 485 — Static widgets in view-mode sections embed two leading spaces in their strings AND inherit .detail-section-body { margin-left: 2 }; net 4-col indent vs intended 2. (3) editor.py:108, 112, 163 — app title format differs across modes ('Edit: id - title' vs 'id: title' vs 'New Issue'). Pick one separator. (4) detail_panel.py:352-357 — Manual checkbox label is one word with no tooltip; users can toggle a flag whose meaning isn't surfaced in the TUI. (5) detail_panel.py:60-65 — ParentPickerScreen height: 24 fixed; ignores tall terminals. Switch to height: auto; min-height: 12; max-height: 80%. (6) detail_panel.py:484-487 — comment timestamps hardcoded UTC %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S, no locale/tz adaptation. (7) detail_panel.py:96 — inline 'from textual.containers import Vertical' inside compose method while module top imports Horizontal/VerticalScroll; inconsistent. (8) detail_panel.py:473 — '\u21b3' (↳) child arrow is a magic literal; not in a STATUS_SYMBOLS-like constant table.

title: TUI: make deps inputs editable inline in detail panel
description: The detail panel renders 'depends-on' / 'blocks' as disabled Input fields with prefix-as-value ("blocked by: a, b"). Users have to drop to the CLI (`dcat update --depends-on`) to change deps. Wire the fields editable in edit mode: drop them from the `_readonly_inputs` set in `enter_edit`, change the rendered value from prefix-style to bare comma-separated IDs ("a, b"), call `_save_dependencies(issue_id)` from `_do_update` after the storage update, and ensure the form re-reads on cancel. The atomic reconcile fix from dogcat-11n6 covers the validation/cycle/partial-commit path that this wiring depends on. Acceptance: pressing 'e' enables both fields; typing a valid id and saving creates the dep; typing an unknown id surfaces a single 'Dependency error: Unknown issue: X' toast and does not partially apply; round-tripping (open, edit, save, reopen) preserves the dep set.
closed_reason: Wired deps inputs editable in enter_edit; placeholders self-describe field; round-trip via _compute_dep_plan + _apply_dep_plan

title: Reduce JSONLStorage load time (startup cost scales with store size)
description:
Every dcat invocation constructs JSONLStorage, which parses the entire .dogcats/issues.jsonl and materializes every Issue object. benchmark.py shows throughput stays at 60-100k issues/sec but total load time grows linearly: ~5ms @ 500 issues, ~122ms @ 10k, ~1.7s @ 100k (120MB file).

Profiling (cProfile, 100k issues) shows where load time goes:
- dict_to_issue (models_serde.py): ~55% — materializing 100k Issue dataclasses
- rebuild_indexes (_indexes.py): ~15-25%
- warn_if_records_from_newer_version (_schema.py): ~180ms — regex version parse per record
- orjson.loads itself is only ~300ms @ 118k lines (the floor)

Also: event records are ~50% of lines in a real store (this repo: 1215 events vs 1221 issue records) and each is fully orjson-parsed just to be skipped; the benchmark contains 0 events so real-world load is worse than benchmarked.

title: Quick wins: cache parse_version and fast-path enum conversion in load path
description:
Two constant-factor optimizations in the hot load path, measured ~30-40% combined at 100k issues:

1. src/dogcat/_schema.py parse_version(): called once per parsed record (118k calls @ 100k issues, ~180ms via find_newest_record_version). Version strings are nearly all identical, so functools.lru_cache on parse_version makes the cost vanish.

2. src/dogcat/models.py _safe_enum(): 215k calls @ 100k issues, each going through Enum.__call__ (~125ms+). Replace with precomputed value->member dict lookups (e.g. Status._value2member_map_ or module-level dicts), falling back to the existing safe behavior for unknown values.

Verify with: uv run ./benchmark.py --counts 10000 100000 -n 3 before/after.
acceptance:
- [ ] parse_version memoized; find_newest_record_version no longer dominates profile
- [ ] _safe_enum uses dict lookup, preserves unknown-value fallback behavior
- [ ] benchmark.py shows measurable improvement at 10k/100k
- [ ] just test-all passes
closed_reason: Implemented: cached parse_version + enum fast path (~3-4% at 100k; corrected measurement on issue). All tests pass.

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text: Implemented: lru_cache(1024) on parse_version (_schema.py), value->member dict fast path in _safe_enum (models.py). CORRECTED MEASUREMENTS: the 30-40% estimate came from cProfile, whose per-call overhead massively inflates tiny hot functions. Honest wall-clock A/B at 100k issues: parse_version cache saves ~30ms (67->38ms in find_newest_record_version), enum fast path saves ~20ms (21->13ms per 100k calls). Total ~3-4% of the ~1.5s load. Real wall-clock phase breakdown at 100k: dict_to_issue 632ms (42%), orjson.loads 436ms (29%), readlines 59ms, version check 37ms, classify 27ms, rebuild_indexes 7ms (cProfile claimed 275ms+ — false). Conclusion: sibling issues dogcat-4mfq (skip event lines pre-parse) and dogcat-4g8d (lazy materialization) are where the real wins are.

title: Skip event lines in _load with byte-level prefilter (no orjson parse)
description:
JSONLStorage._load (src/dogcat/storage.py) fully orjson-parses every event record just to skip it (rtype == 'event' -> continue). Events are ~50% of lines in this repo's own store and grow with every mutation; EventLog already reads them lazily from disk, so _load never needs their contents.

Fix: before orjson.loads, check for the raw byte sequence b'"record_type":"event"' in the stripped line and skip parsing when present. Soundness: orjson writes compact JSON and escapes quotes inside string values, so this exact byte sequence cannot occur inside a string field — it can only be the actual record_type key/value. Files written by other tools with different spacing would just miss the fast path and fall through to the normal parse, which is correct.

Consideration: skipped event lines no longer land in parsed_records, so warn_if_records_from_newer_version (src/dogcat/_schema.py) would not see event-record schema versions. Decide whether that check needs event records (issue/dep/link records almost certainly carry the same writer version) and document the choice.

Verify with a store containing many events (benchmark.py generates none — consider extending it to emit event records so the benchmark reflects real-world files).
acceptance:
- [ ] Event lines skipped without JSON parsing in _load
- [ ] dcat history / EventLog behavior unchanged
- [ ] Version-warning semantics decided and documented
- [ ] Benchmark or test demonstrates improvement on event-heavy files
- [ ] just test-all passes
closed_reason: Implemented: byte-prefix event skip in _load; ~30% faster on event-heavy stores (2197ms -> 1560ms at 100k+185k events). All tests pass.

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text: Implemented: _load skips lines matching EVENT_LINE_PREFIX (b'{"record_type":"event"') via startswith + endswith(b'}') guard, before orjson.loads. Prefix constant lives in event_log.py next to _serialize (which must keep record_type as first key — documented there). Verified all 1222 event lines in this repo's store match the prefix. startswith on the top-level first key cannot be spoofed by nested content (tested: issue with metadata {'record_type': 'event'} still loads). endswith guard keeps truncated event lines (crash mid-append) on the slow path so _bad_lines/_needs_compaction detection still works (tested). Different-key-order events fall through to the correct slow path (tested). Version-check trade-off decided: skipped events are excluded from warn_if_records_from_newer_version; acceptable because every mutation appending an event also appends an issue/dep/link record with the same dcat_version (tested + documented in code comment). benchmark.py now generates realistic event records by default (--no-events to disable; key order matches writer). MEASURED on 100k issues + 185k events (169MB): load 2197ms -> 1560ms min (~30% faster); event lines now cost ~nothing beyond readlines. 1818 affected tests pass.

title: Lazy Issue materialization: keep raw dicts at load, construct Issue on access
description:
dict_to_issue (src/dogcat/models_serde.py) accounts for ~55% of load time at 100k issues — every CLI invocation materializes every Issue dataclass even when the command touches one issue. A measured pickle-snapshot cache is NOT a viable alternative (unpickling still constructs all objects: 547ms load + 528ms index rebuild @ 100k, barely 2x).

Approach: JSONLStorage._load stores the raw parsed dicts (last-write-wins by ID as today) and materializes Issue objects on demand behind an accessor, caching each materialized Issue. rebuild_indexes (src/dogcat/_indexes.py) needs only id/parent from issues plus dep/link records, which read fine off raw dicts.

This is invasive: all code paths touching storage._issues need to go through the accessor. dcat show/update/close then materialize O(1) issues; list/search materialize only what passes filters (or all matching — still a win). Load floor drops to roughly raw orjson parse time (~300ms @ 100k, ~30ms @ 10k).

Do after the two sibling quick-win issues; re-run benchmark.py to quantify.
acceptance:
- [ ] _load stores raw dicts; Issue constructed lazily and cached per ID
- [ ] Index rebuild works from raw dicts
- [ ] No behavior change across CLI/TUI/web (full test suite)
- [ ] benchmark.py load time approaches raw-parse floor
- [ ] just test-all and just lint-all pass
closed_reason: Implemented: LazyIssueMap defers Issue construction to first access; startup 822ms at 100k+events, ID-targeted commands construct O(touched). All tests pass.

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text: Implemented via new LazyIssueMap (src/dogcat/_lazy_issues.py): a MutableMapping[str, Issue] holding one dict whose values are raw record dicts until first __getitem__, which replaces the value with the constructed Issue in place (iteration-safe: value replacement never resizes the dict; identity preserved so in-place mutations by storage code stick). _load validates each record eagerly with precheck_issue_record (models_serde.py) — runs every raising operation of dict_to_issue (required keys, datetime parses, notes type) without constructing objects, so malformed records still land in _bad_lines at load time; a parametrized consistency test in test_models.py pins the two functions together. rebuild_indexes now takes (full_id, parent) pairs via LazyIssueMap.iter_id_parent() so index rebuilds don't materialize. Overrides: __contains__ (Mapping default would materialize per membership test), clear() (MutableMapping default pops via __getitem__). NOTE: renamed the validator to precheck_issue_record because cli/_validate.py already has an unrelated validate_issue_record. benchmark.py now reports startup (constructor) and list (full materialization) separately. MEASURED on 100k issues + 185k events (169MB, realistic store): startup 2197ms (pre-epic) -> 822ms min; dcat-list-style full scan pays +437ms on top. At 10k: startup ~61-85ms, list +45ms. ID-targeted commands (show/update/close) construct O(touched) Issues. just lint-all clean (pyright 0 errors); 3011 tests pass (1 pre-existing repo-data validation failure unrelated to this change, see epic comment).

title: dcat validate flags dangling references in superseded issue records
description:
tests/test_validate.py::TestValidateRepoData::test_repo_issues_jsonl_is_valid fails on this repo's own .dogcats/issues.jsonl with: "Issue dogcat-4vke references non-existent parent 'dogcat-2h7h'".

Root cause: validate_references in src/dogcat/cli/_validate.py checks EVERY issue record in the append-only log — including superseded ones — against the final set of issue IDs. In this store, an old (dcat 0.10.2-era) 4vke record still carries parent dogcat-2h7h, but 2h7h was later pruned; the CURRENT resolved 4vke record (last-write-wins) has parent=None, so the store is healthy. Superseded records are historical noise that the next compaction drops; their references legitimately go stale whenever an issue is pruned or renamed after being referenced.

Fix: validate references against the RESOLVED state (last-write-wins by full id), matching how JSONLStorage._load replays the log. Dependency/link records may need the same treatment if they replay add/remove ops. Structural per-record checks (required fields, timestamps) should stay per-record — only cross-record reference checks move to resolved state.

Regression tests: (1) a store where a superseded record references a now-missing parent but the resolved record does not -> no error; (2) a store where the RESOLVED record references a missing parent -> still an error. The repo-data test then passes without touching .dogcats/issues.jsonl.
acceptance:
- [ ] validate_references checks resolved (last-write-wins) state only
- [ ] Superseded-record dangling refs no longer reported
- [ ] Resolved-record dangling refs still reported
- [ ] tests/test_validate.py::TestValidateRepoData::test_repo_issues_jsonl_is_valid passes
- [ ] just test-all and just lint-all pass
closed_reason: validate_references now checks resolved (last-write-wins) state; repo-data validation test passes, full suite green.

Parent and dependency endpoint checks run on resolved state only; cycle detection uses the resolved edge set; event reference checks unchanged (per-record, warning level). title: Security-headers comment contradicts middleware stacking: 413 responses ship without security headers
description: Comment Cop Red 2 (contradicts-code) - the one finding where the CODE may be the actual bug. src/dogcat/web/propose/__init__.py:212-213 claims the body-size guard runs before security headers so rejected requests still get the standard headers on their 413. Tracing Starlette add_middleware stacking (insert-at-0): BodySizeLimitMiddleware is the OUTER layer and returns its own PlainTextResponse directly on both the Content-Length fast path and the chunked slow path, so 413s never pass through SecurityHeadersMiddleware and carry no security headers. Decide which side is wrong: either fix the comment to state the real behavior, or reorder middleware registration so headers apply to 413s, then re-verify.
acceptance: Either middleware order is changed and a test asserts security headers are present on a 413 response, or the comment states the actual behavior. Decision recorded on this issue.
closed_reason: Comment Cop review follow-up complete; verified just lint-all clean (ruff + pyright 0/0) and 3016 tests pass.

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text: DECISION: the code was the bug, not the comment. Starlette add_middleware inserts at position 0, so the last-registered middleware is outermost. The old order registered SecurityHeadersMiddleware first (inner) and BodySizeLimitMiddleware second (outer), so BodySizeLimit's directly-returned 413 (both the Content-Length fast path and the streamed slow path) never traveled back out through the security-headers layer and shipped bare. Fix: swapped registration so SecurityHeadersMiddleware is outermost; every response, including the 413, now carries X-Content-Type-Options/X-Frame-Options/CSP. This matches the comment's original intent. Added regression test tests/test_web_propose.py::TestBodySizeLimit::test_413_carries_security_headers covering both 413 paths; confirmed it FAILS on the old order and PASSES on the new. This is the one behavior change in the epic (explicitly in scope).

title: comment add: accept -m as alias for --text (or make wrong-flag error suggest -t)
description: git/gh/hg all use -m for messages, so callers reach for 'dcat comment <id> add -m "..."' by reflex. dcat uses -t/--text. The wrong flag exits 2 with a rich 'Error' panel on stderr ('No such option: -m') and the comment is NOT saved. Because the panel header reads 'Error' (no colon) and lands on stderr, batch callers that don't check exit codes miss it: an agent in another repo lost an evening of status comments this way (12 July 2026) before a '--json show' verification revealed 0 comments. Reproduces on v0.12.2 and v0.13.0. Fix options: (a) accept -m as an alias for --text on comment add, or (b) special-case the wrong-flag error on comment add to suggest -t. Option (a) removes the trap entirely.

title: Global-config walk-up warning fires on every command against an intended shared store (noise + corrupts --json under 2>&1)
description: The global-config feature exists to point .dogcatrc at a shared store OUTSIDE the repo, yet warn_if_rc_target_foreign (config.py:138) treats 'outside the rc's directory' as suspicious and prints a stderr warning on EVERY command. So the supported, intended setup produces perpetual noise; the only escape is setting DCAT_RC_WALKUP_UNRESTRICTED=1 in every environment. Worse: because the warning fires constantly on stderr, any caller doing 'dcat --json ... 2>&1 | parse' (a common agent pattern) gets JSONDecodeError even though the command succeeded. Verified on v0.13.0. Fix direction: do not warn when the rc target is a deliberately-configured global store (e.g. it matches the user-global config default_storage), and/or add a per-rc trust marker so it is silenced once instead of via a global env var. NB: --json output itself IS clean JSON on stdout (verified v0.12.2 and v0.13.0); the earlier belief that '--json create/list' emit dirty JSON was a misdiagnosis of this stderr-merge issue.

title.new: Add dcat hook install/uninstall/list commands for Claude Code hooks

description.new:
Add CLI commands to manage Claude Code hooks in .claude/settings.local.json.

## Commands

### dcat hook install <name> [options]
Installs a named hook into .claude/settings.local.json. Creates the file or merges into existing structure. Idempotent — skips with a message if already present.

Available hooks:
- sessionStart: SessionStart event, matcher 'startup|resume|clear', runs 'dcat prime'. With --opinionated flag, runs 'dcat prime --opinionated' instead.
- preCompact: PreCompact event, matcher '' (all), runs 'dcat prime --replay'.

### dcat hook uninstall <name>
Removes the named hook from .claude/settings.local.json. Cleans up empty hooks/event arrays after removal.

### dcat hook list
Shows installed hooks from .claude/settings.local.json. Also shows hooks from .claude/settings.json marked as '(shared)'.

## Edge cases
- No .claude/settings.local.json exists → create it
- File exists but no hooks key → add it
- Hook already installed → no-op with message
- Uninstall hook that isn't installed → no-op with message

## Tab completions
Add autocompletion callbacks for hook names (sessionStart, preCompact) on install and uninstall subcommands, per project conventions.

title.new: Reduce JSONLStorage load time (startup cost scales with store size)

description.new:
Every dcat invocation constructs JSONLStorage, which parses the entire .dogcats/issues.jsonl and materializes every Issue object. benchmark.py shows throughput stays at 60-100k issues/sec but total load time grows linearly: ~5ms @ 500 issues, ~122ms @ 10k, ~1.7s @ 100k (120MB file).

Profiling (cProfile, 100k issues) shows where load time goes:
- dict_to_issue (models_serde.py): ~55% — materializing 100k Issue dataclasses
- rebuild_indexes (_indexes.py): ~15-25%
- warn_if_records_from_newer_version (_schema.py): ~180ms — regex version parse per record
- orjson.loads itself is only ~300ms @ 118k lines (the floor)

Also: event records are ~50% of lines in a real store (this repo: 1215 events vs 1221 issue records) and each is fully orjson-parsed just to be skipped; the benchmark contains 0 events so real-world load is worse than benchmarked.

Constraint: SQLite/embedded-DB read models are off the table (project goal). All fixes stay within the JSONL architecture. Floor after all child issues: roughly the orjson parse cost of live records (~300ms @ 100k, ~30ms @ 10k).

Child issues cover: (1) constant-factor quick wins, (2) byte-level prefilter to skip event lines before JSON parsing, (3) lazy Issue materialization.

description.new:
Two constant-factor optimizations in the hot load path, measured ~30-40% combined at 100k issues:

1. src/dogcat/_schema.py parse_version(): called once per parsed record (118k calls @ 100k issues, ~180ms via find_newest_record_version). Version strings are nearly all identical, so functools.lru_cache on parse_version makes the cost vanish.

2. src/dogcat/models.py _safe_enum(): 215k calls @ 100k issues, each going through Enum.__call__ (~125ms+). Replace with precomputed value->member dict lookups (e.g. Status._value2member_map_ or module-level dicts), falling back to the existing safe behavior for unknown values.

Verify with: uv run ./benchmark.py --counts 10000 100000 -n 3 before/after.

title: Quick wins: cache parse_version and fast-path enum conversion in load path

description.new:
JSONLStorage._load (src/dogcat/storage.py) fully orjson-parses every event record just to skip it (rtype == 'event' -> continue). Events are ~50% of lines in this repo's own store and grow with every mutation; EventLog already reads them lazily from disk, so _load never needs their contents.

Fix: before orjson.loads, check for the raw byte sequence b'"record_type":"event"' in the stripped line and skip parsing when present. Soundness: orjson writes compact JSON and escapes quotes inside string values, so this exact byte sequence cannot occur inside a string field — it can only be the actual record_type key/value. Files written by other tools with different spacing would just miss the fast path and fall through to the normal parse, which is correct.

Consideration: skipped event lines no longer land in parsed_records, so warn_if_records_from_newer_version (src/dogcat/_schema.py) would not see event-record schema versions. Decide whether that check needs event records (issue/dep/link records almost certainly carry the same writer version) and document the choice.

Verify with a store containing many events (benchmark.py generates none — consider extending it to emit event records so the benchmark reflects real-world files).

description.new:
dict_to_issue (src/dogcat/models_serde.py) accounts for ~55% of load time at 100k issues — every CLI invocation materializes every Issue dataclass even when the command touches one issue. A measured pickle-snapshot cache is NOT a viable alternative (unpickling still constructs all objects: 547ms load + 528ms index rebuild @ 100k, barely 2x).

Approach: JSONLStorage._load stores the raw parsed dicts (last-write-wins by ID as today) and materializes Issue objects on demand behind an accessor, caching each materialized Issue. rebuild_indexes (src/dogcat/_indexes.py) needs only id/parent from issues plus dep/link records, which read fine off raw dicts.

This is invasive: all code paths touching storage._issues need to go through the accessor. dcat show/update/close then materialize O(1) issues; list/search materialize only what passes filters (or all matching — still a win). Load floor drops to roughly raw orjson parse time (~300ms @ 100k, ~30ms @ 10k).

Do after the two sibling quick-win issues; re-run benchmark.py to quantify.

title.new: dcat validate flags dangling references in superseded issue records

description.new:
tests/test_validate.py::TestValidateRepoData::test_repo_issues_jsonl_is_valid fails on this repo's own .dogcats/issues.jsonl with: "Issue dogcat-4vke references non-existent parent 'dogcat-2h7h'".

Root cause: validate_references in src/dogcat/cli/_validate.py checks EVERY issue record in the append-only log — including superseded ones — against the final set of issue IDs. In this store, an old (dcat 0.10.2-era) 4vke record still carries parent dogcat-2h7h, but 2h7h was later pruned; the CURRENT resolved 4vke record (last-write-wins) has parent=None, so the store is healthy. Superseded records are historical noise that the next compaction drops; their references legitimately go stale whenever an issue is pruned or renamed after being referenced.

Fix: validate references against the RESOLVED state (last-write-wins by full id), matching how JSONLStorage._load replays the log. Dependency/link records may need the same treatment if they replay add/remove ops. Structural per-record checks (required fields, timestamps) should stay per-record — only cross-record reference checks move to resolved state.

Regression tests: (1) a store where a superseded record references a now-missing parent but the resolved record does not -> no error; (2) a store where the RESOLVED record references a missing parent -> still an error. The repo-data test then passes without touching .dogcats/issues.jsonl.

description.new: Comment Cop Red 2 (contradicts-code) - the one finding where the CODE may be the actual bug. src/dogcat/web/propose/__init__.py:212-213 claims the body-size guard runs before security headers so rejected requests still get the standard headers on their 413. Tracing Starlette add_middleware stacking (insert-at-0): BodySizeLimitMiddleware is the OUTER layer and returns its own PlainTextResponse directly on both the Content-Length fast path and the chunked slow path, so 413s never pass through SecurityHeadersMiddleware and carry no security headers. Decide which side is wrong: either fix the comment to state the real behavior, or reorder middleware registration so headers apply to 413s, then re-verify.

title.new: comment add: accept -m as alias for --text (or make wrong-flag error suggest -t)

description.new: git/gh/hg all use -m for messages, so callers reach for 'dcat comment <id> add -m "..."' by reflex. dcat uses -t/--text. The wrong flag exits 2 with a rich 'Error' panel on stderr ('No such option: -m') and the comment is NOT saved. Because the panel header reads 'Error' (no colon) and lands on stderr, batch callers that don't check exit codes miss it: an agent in another repo lost an evening of status comments this way (12 July 2026) before a '--json show' verification revealed 0 comments. Reproduces on v0.12.2 and v0.13.0. Fix options: (a) accept -m as an alias for --text on comment add, or (b) special-case the wrong-flag error on comment add to suggest -t. Option (a) removes the trap entirely.

title.new: Global-config walk-up warning fires on every command against an intended shared store (noise + corrupts --json under 2>&1)

description.new: The global-config feature exists to point .dogcatrc at a shared store OUTSIDE the repo, yet warn_if_rc_target_foreign (config.py:138) treats 'outside the rc's directory' as suspicious and prints a stderr warning on EVERY command. So the supported, intended setup produces perpetual noise; the only escape is setting DCAT_RC_WALKUP_UNRESTRICTED=1 in every environment. Worse: because the warning fires constantly on stderr, any caller doing 'dcat --json ... 2>&1 | parse' (a common agent pattern) gets JSONDecodeError even though the command succeeded. Verified on v0.13.0. Fix direction: do not warn when the rc target is a deliberately-configured global store (e.g. it matches the user-global config default_storage), and/or add a per-rc trust marker so it is silenced once instead of via a global env var. NB: --json output itself IS clean JSON on stdout (verified v0.12.2 and v0.13.0); the earlier belief that '--json create/list' emit dirty JSON was a misdiagnosis of this stderr-merge issue.

Bump action-gh-release to v3 and drop FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24 workaround
description:
GitHub Actions emits a deprecation annotation on the Publish Release workflow: "Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: softprops/action-gh-release@v2."

Root cause: both .github/workflows/publish.yml (line 83) and .github/workflows/release.yml (line 58) pin softprops/action-gh-release@v2, whose action.yml still declares `using: "node20"`. Both workflows set an env workaround `FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: true` (publish.yml:12-13, release.yml:11-12) that forces the node20 action onto the node24 runtime. Releases currently succeed, but the warning persists and the force-flag is a stopgap that will break once GitHub removes Node 20 from runners.

Upstream shipped v3 on 2026-04-12 (latest v3.0.2). v3.0.0 is purely a Node 20 to Node 24 runtime bump with no input/API changes. Our usage (tag_name, name, body, files, prerelease) is unaffected. Verified: @v2 action.yml uses node20; @v3 uses node24.
acceptance:
- softprops/action-gh-release pinned to @v3 in both publish.yml and release.yml
- FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24 env block removed from both workflows (native node24 makes it redundant)
- Node 20 deprecation annotation no longer appears on the next release run
- No other workflow behavior changes
notes: v3 is a new major tag; the only change vs v2 is the node24 runtime bump (per upstream v3.0.0 release notes). Safe drop-in for our simple usage.

description:
Supply-chain hardening: pin all remaining third-party GitHub Actions to full commit SHAs (with a trailing version comment) and bump to latest, then add Dependabot so the pins don't go stale.

Actions and resolved targets (verified via gh api; breaking changes checked against our usage — none affect us):
- actions/checkout @v5 -> 9c091bb21b7c1c1d1991bb908d89e4e9dddfe3e0 # v7.0.0 (v7 fork-PR block only affects pull_request_target/workflow_run, which we don't use; v6 added node24)
- astral-sh/setup-uv @v7 -> 11f9893b081a58869d3b5fccaea48c9e9e46f990 # v8.3.2 (v8 removes floating major tags and a deprecated manifest-file format we don't use; we pass no inputs)
- pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish @release/v1 (moving branch) -> cef221092ed1bacb1cc03d23a2d87d1d172e277b # v1.14.0 (same major; pinning freezes the tracking branch)

Files: .github/workflows/{ci,publish,release,validate-issues}.yml. checkout appears in all four; setup-uv in all four; pypi-publish only in publish.yml.

Also add .github/dependabot.yml (github-actions ecosystem, weekly, grouped) so pinned SHAs get automated update PRs — the standard mitigation for SHA pinning going stale.

Bump action-gh-release to v3 and drop FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24 workaround
description:
GitHub Actions emits a deprecation annotation on the Publish Release workflow: "Node.js 20 is deprecated. The following actions target Node.js 20 but are being forced to run on Node.js 24: softprops/action-gh-release@v2."

Root cause: both .github/workflows/publish.yml (line 83) and .github/workflows/release.yml (line 58) pin softprops/action-gh-release@v2, whose action.yml still declares `using: "node20"`. Both workflows set an env workaround `FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: true` (publish.yml:12-13, release.yml:11-12) that forces the node20 action onto the node24 runtime. Releases currently succeed, but the warning persists and the force-flag is a stopgap that will break once GitHub removes Node 20 from runners.

Upstream shipped v3 on 2026-04-12 (latest v3.0.2). v3.0.0 is purely a Node 20 to Node 24 runtime bump with no input/API changes. Our usage (tag_name, name, body, files, prerelease) is unaffected. Verified: @v2 action.yml uses node20; @v3 uses node24.

Take py_project_template's ruff rule families
description:
Colophon's ruff-rules-behind-template check flagged dogcat as the last repo in the fleet not selecting the template's full rule set: ASYNC, FA, FBT, PL, S, T20 were missing from [tool.ruff.lint] select in pyproject.toml.

Selecting them raised 7357 violations. Layer by layer: 1902 with the template's tests/** per-file-ignores, 1068 with the template's ignore list too, and 199 once PLC0415 (import-outside-top-level) was also ignored -- so 869 of the 1068 were PLC0415 alone.

The PLC0415 question was the crux and was settled with a measurement rather than a guess. Those deferred imports are load-bearing: 'import dogcat.cli' pulls in no textual, fastapi or uvicorn module, because each import sits inside the function that needs it, and 'python -X importtime' puts textual.app alone at ~360ms against dogcat.cli's ~605ms. Hoisting them to module scope would roughly double what every dcat invocation pays. Several also break import cycles inside cli/. PLC0415 is therefore ignored with that reasoning recorded inline in pyproject.toml.

PLR0912 (too-many-branches) joins C901 in the ignore list -- the same complaint, already settled here on the same grounds ('CLI commands are inherently complex'). Reducing 35 functions' branch counts, led by doctor at 56, is a refactor project rather than a lint-config change.

tests/** additionally ignores S603/S607 (the suite drives real git with fixed argv to build repo fixtures), S108 ('/tmp/...' strings fed to path parsing, never opened) and PLE2502 (test_storage.py must literally contain bidi control characters to pin their round-trip, dogcat-2rpd). The src-side subprocess calls carry per-line noqa instead, matching the pattern colophon and control_panel3 settled on.

The rest were fixed rather than ignored: PLW2901 loop-variable rebinding, PLR5501 else/if collapsed to elif, explicit check=False where the returncode is inspected (PLW1510), and assorted PLR1714/PLC0206/PLC0207/PLW0108 cleanups.

Landed as commit ba7b5be on main. This issue is filed after the fact so dogcat's own tracker records the decision; the driving issue was colophon-59t5.
acceptance: pyproject.toml selects ASYNC, FA, FBT, PL, S and T20; the PLC0415 decision is recorded inline with its rationale; 'just lint-all' and 'just test' both pass. Verified: ruff clean, ruff format clean, pyright 0 errors 0 warnings, 2676 passed / 2 skipped.

title: Take py_project_template's ruff rule families
Swap eslint for oxlint/oxfmt to match the template
description:
dogcat's justfile still shells out to eslint for the web static JS, but eslint is not actually installed in the working environment -- 'just lint' and 'just fmt' both print 'sh: eslint: command not found' and continue, so the JS lint step has been silently doing nothing.

Meanwhile py_project_template has moved to oxlint/oxfmt (oxc), and colophon, timebank and radgiver have all followed. dogcat is the odd one out.

Current state in dogcat:
- justfile:16 (fmt): 'eslint --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern --fix src/dogcat/web/**/static/**/*js'
- justfile:22 (lint): 'eslint --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern src/dogcat/web/**/static/**/*js'
- package.json devDependencies: eslint ^9.39.1, @eslint/js ^9.39.1, plus stylelint ^16.16.0 and stylelint-config-standard ^38.0.0
- No .oxlintrc.json

Reference configs to copy from, in order of authority:
- py_project_template/templates/justfile.j2 and templates/package.json.j2 -- the canonical recipes
- py_project_template/templates/.oxlintrc.json -- the canonical rule config
- radgiver is the only fleet repo that also has a .oxfmtrc.json, so check whether oxfmt needs config here or runs on defaults

Note the glob in the existing recipes is '*js' rather than '*.js', which would also miss files; carry the template's glob rather than the current one.

Open question worth settling while in here: whether stylelint stays or the CSS also moves to an oxc-based check. The template's package.json.j2 is the reference for what the fleet expects.
acceptance: dogcat runs oxlint (and oxfmt where the template does) instead of eslint, with .oxlintrc.json matching py_project_template's. eslint and @eslint/js are removed from package.json. 'just lint' and 'just fmt' both run the JS step for real -- no 'command not found' -- and pass. Committed and pushed.

fleet-dogcat-typer-private-click: Replace the private typer._click import with a supported type
description:
Bumping typer 0.24.1 -> 0.27.1 (commit ab42251, dogcat-1sxv) forced dogcat to reference **typer._click**, a private module with no stability guarantee, in two places:

- `src/dogcat/cli/_helpers.py` — `from typer._click import Context as ClickContext` inside the `TYPE_CHECKING` block, used to annotate `SortedGroup.list_commands(self, ctx: ClickContext)`. Type-only, so a future typer reshuffle breaks pyright rather than runtime.
- `tests/test_cmd_list.py` — `import typer._click` and `typer._click.Context(group)` in `TestCLICommandOrder.test_commands_are_alphabetically_sorted`. This one is a **runtime** import: if the module moves, the test fails outright.

Why it ended up this way: typer 0.27 vendors its own click fork, so `TyperGroup.list_commands` now takes a `typer._click.Context`. Annotating with the `click` package no longer type-checks, and the public `typer.Context` is a *subclass* — using it would narrow the override and violate LSP. The vendored base was the only accurate type available at the time.

Investigate whether there is a supported way to express this:
- Does typer re-export the vendored Context under any public name (check `typer.__init__`, `typer.core`, release notes for 0.25-0.27)?
- Can the override drop the annotation entirely and inherit the base signature, keeping pyright happy without naming the module?
- If nothing public exists, is upstream willing to export one? Worth an issue on fastapi/typer.

Acceptance criteria:
Either no reference to `typer._click` remains under src/ or tests/ and `just lint-all` is clean (pyright included) with the suite still green; or the investigation concludes no supported alternative exists, that finding is recorded in this issue, and the two call sites carry a comment naming the constraint and the typer version it was verified against.

Add --include-history flag to dcat show
description:
Users want the issue's audit trail inline with its details instead of running a second command.

Today: `dcat show <id>` prints issue details; `dcat history --issue <id>` prints the event timeline separately.

Add `--include-history` to `dcat show` (src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_read.py, show command at ~line 765). When set, append a History section after each issue's rendered block, using the same event rendering as the history command (format_event / get_event_legend in src/dogcat/cli/_formatting.py, event loading via EventLog in src/dogcat/event_log.py, see src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_history.py for the reference implementation).

Design decisions:
- Show ALL events for the issue by default (no limit) — an issue's audit trail is small enough that silent truncation is worse than length.
- Events display oldest-first (chronological), matching `dcat history`.
- In --json mode, embed the serialized events as a nested `history` array on the issue object rather than printing a separate stream.
- Works with multiple issue IDs: each issue gets its own history section.
- No autocompletion needed (boolean flag).
acceptance:
- `dcat show <id> --include-history` prints issue details followed by a History section with all events for that issue, oldest-first
- `dcat show <id>` without the flag is byte-identical to current output
- `dcat show <id> --include-history --json` emits the issue dict with a `history` key holding serialized events
- `dcat show <a> <b> --include-history` renders a history section per issue
- Issue with no events shows a clear empty message rather than a bare header
- Tests cover: flag on/off, JSON shape, multi-ID, and empty history
- `just lint-all` and `just test-all` pass

Add handoff-question convention to prime's opinionated rules
description:
Agents hand work back by listing open decisions as prose questions at the end of a message ("want me to do X? And can I close Y?"). That bundling forces one combined answer — the user loses the ability to answer each decision differently — and yes/no phrasing hides what each choice actually changes.

Add a rule to the --opinionated block in src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py (the `opinionated_rules` string, ~line 937) covering how agents ask for decisions:

- Use a structured question tool (AskUserQuestion in Claude Code) rather than trailing prose questions.
- One question per decision. Never bundle two decisions into one question.
- List the open decisions in prose first, then ask them one at a time.
- Option labels state the change in 1-5 words, not yes/no. Put the recommended option first and mark it.

Note the blast radius: prime output ships to every dogcat user, so word the rule tool-agnostically — say 'a structured question tool' rather than naming one vendor's tool, and keep it within the existing terse style of the surrounding rules (two-space indent, wrapped at the same width).

This rule already exists as user preference in this session; encoding it in prime makes it survive compaction, /clear, and fresh sessions.
acceptance:
- `dcat prime --opinionated` prints the new rule under ## Rules
- `dcat prime` without --opinionated is unchanged
- Wording is tool-agnostic (no vendor tool name) and matches the surrounding indent/width style
- Existing prime tests still pass; a test asserts the new rule appears only in opinionated output
- `just lint-all` and `just test-all` pass

Add handoff-question convention to prime's opinionated rules
description:
Agents hand work back by listing open decisions as prose questions at the end of a message ("want me to do X? And can I close Y?"). That bundling forces one combined answer — the user loses the ability to answer each decision differently — and yes/no phrasing hides what each choice actually changes.

Add a rule to the --opinionated block in src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py (the `opinionated_rules` string, ~line 937) covering how agents ask for decisions:

- Use a structured question tool (AskUserQuestion in Claude Code) rather than trailing prose questions.
- One question per decision. Never bundle two decisions into one question.
- List the open decisions in prose first, then ask them one at a time.
- Option labels state the change in 1-5 words, not yes/no. Put the recommended option first and mark it.

Note the blast radius: prime output ships to every dogcat user, so word the rule tool-agnostically — say 'a structured question tool' rather than naming one vendor's tool, and keep it within the existing terse style of the surrounding rules (two-space indent, wrapped at the same width).

This rule already exists as user preference in this session; encoding it in prime makes it survive compaction, /clear, and fresh sessions.
acceptance:
- `dcat prime --opinionated` prints the new rule under ## Rules
- `dcat prime` without --opinionated is unchanged
- Wording is tool-agnostic (no vendor tool name) and matches the surrounding indent/width style
- Existing prime tests still pass; a test asserts the new rule appears only in opinionated output
- `just lint-all` and `just test-all` pass

Close remaining agent-doc audit gaps: merge-coverage status rows and enforcement layer
description:
Three findings from the agent-doc audit were left unfixed because each needs a decision or a new enforcement layer rather than a doc edit.

1. docs/merge-coverage.md status rows. Two rows are marked green but their cited tests never construct the case the claim hinges on: "Deterministic: fixed ours/theirs produce the same result" (test_same_issue_latest_wins uses distinct timestamps 2026-01-02 vs 2026-01-03, so the new_ts >= old_ts equal-timestamp tie-break at merge_driver.py:405 is untested) and "Convergent across argument order" (test_issue_convergence merges from an empty base, so it never builds the equal-updated_at same-ID case). Both should become partial with the caveat stated.

2. Two missing gap rows in the same file. The module docstring asserts a status rank draft < open/in_progress/in_review/blocked/deferred < closed < tombstone (_ISSUE_STATUS_RANK, merge_driver.py:309-318), but no test covers the draft rank or the five-active-status equivalence -- grep draft over the merge tests returns nothing. Separately, .dogcats/archive/*.jsonl is tracked in git but the .gitattributes pattern .dogcats/*.jsonl does not cross a directory separator, so archive files merge with git default text driver and can take conflict markers (git check-attr merge on an archive file returns "unspecified"). Either widen the pattern to .dogcats/**/*.jsonl or document manual resolution. A gap row needs an issue id, which is why these were not written during the audit fix.

3. No enforcement layer behind the guardrails. This repo has no .claude/ directory, so every rule in AGENTS.md is advisory prose. Two candidates: a permissions.deny list in .claude/settings.json covering the destructive commands AGENTS.md names (dcat prune, dcat archive, dcat repair-jsonl, dcat backfill-history, git push --force, git reset --hard, just release-prep), and hooks replacing the prose lint/test gates (a PostToolUse hook running just fmt after edits, a PreToolUse hook running just lint-all and just test-all before commit). Prose gates only fire when the model remembers them.

A gap row exists for the draft status rank and for .dogcats/archive/*.jsonl, each carrying this issue id or a follow-up id. Close remaining agent-doc audit gaps: merge-coverage status rows and enforcement layer
description:
Three findings from the agent-doc audit were left unfixed because each needs a decision or a new enforcement layer rather than a doc edit.

1. docs/merge-coverage.md status rows. Two rows are marked green but their cited tests never construct the case the claim hinges on: "Deterministic: fixed ours/theirs produce the same result" (test_same_issue_latest_wins uses distinct timestamps 2026-01-02 vs 2026-01-03, so the new_ts >= old_ts equal-timestamp tie-break at merge_driver.py:405 is untested) and "Convergent across argument order" (test_issue_convergence merges from an empty base, so it never builds the equal-updated_at same-ID case). Both should become partial with the caveat stated.

2. Two missing gap rows in the same file. The module docstring asserts a status rank draft < open/in_progress/in_review/blocked/deferred < closed < tombstone (_ISSUE_STATUS_RANK, merge_driver.py:309-318), but no test covers the draft rank or the five-active-status equivalence -- grep draft over the merge tests returns nothing. Separately, .dogcats/archive/*.jsonl is tracked in git but the .gitattributes pattern .dogcats/*.jsonl does not cross a directory separator, so archive files merge with git default text driver and can take conflict markers (git check-attr merge on an archive file returns "unspecified"). Either widen the pattern to .dogcats/**/*.jsonl or document manual resolution. A gap row needs an issue id, which is why these were not written during the audit fix.

3. No enforcement layer behind the guardrails. This repo has no .claude/ directory, so every rule in AGENTS.md is advisory prose. Two candidates: a permissions.deny list in .claude/settings.json covering the destructive commands AGENTS.md names (dcat prune, dcat archive, dcat repair-jsonl, dcat backfill-history, git push --force, git reset --hard, just release-prep), and hooks replacing the prose lint/test gates (a PostToolUse hook running just fmt after edits, a PreToolUse hook running just lint-all and just test-all before commit). Prose gates only fire when the model remembers them.
acceptance: The two hedged rows in docs/merge-coverage.md read partial with the caveat spelled out. A gap row exists for the draft status rank and for .dogcats/archive/*.jsonl, each carrying this issue id or a follow-up id. A decision is recorded on whether .claude/settings.json and hooks are wanted; if yes, they exist and are verified.

Comment Cop sweep: fix misleading, rotting, and redundant prose across the codebase
description:
Umbrella for the findings of a Comment Cop review run on 2026-08-09 against branch docs260809 (commit a75488f). Ten reviewer lenses (contradicts-code, rambling, transient, restates-code, missing-why, dead-comments, docstring-gaps, doc-drift, noise, llm-slop) analysed a 581KB prose-dense snapshot of src/dogcat, docs/, README.md, AGENTS.md, the web assets, and a sample of tests. Findings were deduplicated and ranked by a distillation pass.

Scope is the documentation layer only: comments, docstrings, and prose docs. No child issue here asks for a behaviour change. Where a docstring is wrong because the code has a real gap (see the child on models.py strip_control_chars), the fix is to state the truth in the prose; any code change is a separate issue.

Children are grouped by tier:
- Red (priority 1): prose that misleads a maintainer into a bug or misstates a safety-critical property.
- Yellow (priority 2): docstrings contradicting code, doc drift, rot-prone anecdotes, API docstring gaps.
- Green (priority 3): rambling, restatements, decorative noise.

Two constraints that apply to every child:
1. pyproject.toml enables ruff's full D (pydocstyle) family, so a public docstring cannot simply be deleted without failing just lint. For docstring findings the action is replace-the-echo-with-the-missing-fact, never delete.
2. AGENTS.md declares src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_example_md.py, src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py and README.md deliberate near-duplicate product surface. Changing one means checking the other two.

Acceptance: every child closed or explicitly deferred, and just lint-all plus just test-all pass.

Merge-driver prose claims git falls back to its default merge on exit 1 — it does not
description:
Three sites say the merge driver exits 1 'so git falls back to its default merge strategy'. That is false. Git treats a non-zero merge-driver exit as a conflict on that path: it leaves the ours-side file (%A) exactly as it was and marks the path conflicted. No fallback merge runs. AGENTS.md already documents the real behaviour ('the file holds ours-side content only — staging it discards the other branch's issues'), so the source contradicts the repo's own guardrail doc.

Cost: the log message at _cmd_docs.py:481 is what a user sees at the exact moment the driver fails. It reassures them that git handled it, so they stage the file and silently drop every issue from the other branch.

Sites:
- src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py:444 — command docstring
- src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py:481 — user-facing log line
- tests/test_merge_driver.py:766 — test docstring ('exits 1 so git falls back'), which is what a maintainer reads when deciding the exit code is safe
acceptance: All three sites state that git marks the path conflicted and keeps ours-side content. The word 'falls back' appears at none of them. The log line warns against staging the file blindly. No behaviour change: the driver still exits 1.

Document why InboxStorage._append has no should_compact check — copying the sibling would erase the inbox event log
description:
JSONLStorage._append runs a should_compact() check that can trigger a full rewrite. InboxStorage._append does not, and that omission is load-bearing: InboxStorage._save_locked serializes only proposal records, so any rewrite of inbox.jsonl drops every event record the shared emitter appended. JSONLStorage._save_locked preserves events via compact_snapshot, so the parallel class names read as an accidental inconsistency rather than a deliberate divergence.

Cost: a maintainer restoring parity between the two _append methods destroys inbox history, and nothing in the file warns them. The fact currently lives only in docs/web-ui.md, which nobody reads while editing inbox.py.

Sites:
- src/dogcat/inbox.py:189 (_append) — needs the do-not-add-compaction warning
- src/dogcat/inbox.py:166/171 (_save / _save_locked) — needs the proposals-only rewrite statement and the explicit contrast with JSONLStorage._save_locked
acceptance: inbox.py states at both sites that the rewrite is proposals-only, that it therefore drops event records, that this diverges from JSONLStorage._save_locked on purpose, and that _append must not gain a should_compact branch. No behaviour change.

acceptance.new: inbox.py states at both sites that the rewrite is proposals-only, that it therefore drops event records, that this diverges from JSONLStorage._save_locked on purpose, and that _append must not gain a should_compact branch. No behaviour change.

_resolve_dogcats_path docstring claims parity with the hardened walk-up it does not implement
description:
src/dogcat/config.py:611 — _resolve_dogcats_path walks up from the cwd looking for a .dogcatrc and accepts the first one it finds. Its docstring says it 'mirrors the walk-up logic in cli._helpers.find_dogcats_dir'. It does not. The real walk-up applies get_rc_walkup_boundary and refuse_if_rc_target_cross_user; this copy is unbounded to the filesystem root, applies no cross-user refusal, and swallows a malformed rc with 'except ValueError: pass'. Both sibling walk-ups (_find_rc_parent in this same file, walkup_find_store in cli/_helpers.py) carry explicit rationale for those guards.

Cost: the word 'mirrors' tells a reader the hardening is present. It is not, so a planted /tmp/.dogcatrc can steer namespace resolution through this path without hitting the defense the other path enforces.

Scope note: prose only. If the missing guards are a real defect rather than a deliberate exemption, that is a separate issue — this one just makes the docstring tell the truth.
acceptance: The docstring no longer claims parity. It states that this walk is unbounded and applies no cross-user refusal, unlike _find_rc_parent and walkup_find_store, and either gives the reason it is safe here or says the rationale is unknown. No behaviour change.
