Explain the or-not-and archive filter in storage.py before someone 'fixes' it
description:
src/dogcat/storage.py:1674 and :1680 filter in-memory dependencies and links after an archive rewrite with:

    if dep.issue_id not in archived_ids or dep.depends_on_id not in archived_ids

The 'or' reads like an 'and' typo. It is not: it is the De Morgan inverse of classify_archived_line's rule that an edge is archived only when BOTH endpoints are archived. A half-archived edge stays in issues.jsonl, so it must stay in memory too.

Cost: changing it to 'and' drops in-memory edges whose surviving endpoint is still live, desyncing memory from the file that was just rewritten. Nothing at either call site records the constraint, so the 'fix' looks obviously correct.

Sites: src/dogcat/storage.py:1674, :1680
acceptance: Both sites carry a comment stating that 'or' is deliberate, that it mirrors classify_archived_line's both-endpoints rule, and what breaks if it becomes 'and'. No behaviour change.

with_ns_shim docstring describes a global-callback mechanism that does not exist
description:
src/dogcat/cli/_helpers.py:43 — the 'why' paragraph on with_ns_shim says the --namespace / --all-namespaces flags are 'owned by the global Typer callback' and that 'the actual filter is applied by get_namespace_filter() reading the process state set by the global callback'.

None of that is true. The global callback in cli/__init__.py declares only --json and -C/--repo. No namespace process state exists. get_namespace_filter() reads config plus an explicit argument. The shim kwargs.pop()s both values and discards them, so 'dcat close ID --namespace ns' parses fine and filters nothing.

What the shim actually buys: the command parses the options without error, and _ns_filter_from_ctx (cli/_completions.py:20) can read them off the Click context during tab completion.

Cost: a reader debugging why --namespace has no effect on a mutation command is sent to a callback that never touches namespaces.

description:
src/dogcat/merge_driver.py:519 — the merge_jsonl docstring enumerates the four record kinds it merges but never says what happens to anything else. CLI root callback has no docstring for its three process-wide side effects
description:
src/dogcat/cli/__init__.py:21 — the Typer root callback is the entry point for every dcat invocation and has no docstring. The leading underscore exempts it from ruff's D103, so lint never asked for one.

Three undocumented behaviours, all process-wide:
1. -C/--repo resolves the path strictly and calls os.chdir() on the process before any subcommand runs, exiting 1 if the path is missing or not a directory.
2. --json resets and sets module-global JSON state that every command reads via is_json().
3. A bare 'dcat' with no subcommand prints help and exits 0.

Cost: anyone adding a command or writing a test against the CLI has to read the body to learn that the process cwd moves under them.
acceptance: The callback carries a docstring covering all three behaviours, naming os.chdir() and the global JSON state explicitly. No behaviour change.

description:
Line-number citations in prose rot on the first edit above the cited line. Five are already wrong, and three reviewer lenses caught them independently:

- docs/web-ui.md:25 — cites constants.py:291 for the CSP string; WEB_CSP_HEADER is at constants.py:305, and 291 lands inside an unrelated declaration.
- docs/cli-conventions.md:17 — cites _cmd_config.py:39 for _KNOWN_KEYS; it is at :42, and 39 is the closing brace of _ARRAY_KEYS, so a reader edits the wrong constant.
- docs/cli-conventions.md:50 — cites _cmd_chart.py:146 for _complete_by_values; defined at :150.
- docs/merge-coverage.md:28 — cites merge_driver.py:309-318 for _ISSUE_STATUS_RANK; the dict spans 311-320, so the cited range starts mid-comment and cuts off 'tombstone' — the highest rank, which is exactly what that row's finality argument rests on.
- tests/test_merge_driver.py:352 — same wrong 309-318 range.

Preferred fix is to drop the numbers entirely and cite the symbol name, which is grep-able and cannot rot. Note that four further citations elsewhere in these docs are currently correct; converting all of them to symbol names in the same pass stops the whole class of finding recurring.
acceptance: No wrong line citation remains. Either the five ranges are corrected or, preferably, the file:line form is replaced by symbol names throughout the docs set.

Store-resolution order in docs/sharing-a-database.md contradicts walkup_find_store and omits the worktree step
description:
docs/sharing-a-database.md:133 numbers the resolution order as: step 1 'Local .dogcats/ in the current directory', step 2 walk up checking .dogcatrc then .dogcats/ 'at each ancestor directory', step 3 fall back to the global default.

The real loop (walkup_find_store, cli/_helpers.py:282-304) checks .dogcatrc before .dogcats/ at EVERY level including the cwd — one pass, cwd treated no differently from an ancestor. get_storage even carries a comment saying exactly this: 'Always resolve via find_dogcats_dir() to respect .dogcatrc priority over a local .dogcats/ directory (which may only contain config.local.toml)'. So step 1 contradicts step 2, and contradicts this doc's own example layout where every app repo holds both a .dogcatrc and a .dogcats/config.local.toml.

Cost: a reader debugging 'why isn't my repo using the shared store?' concludes from step 1 that the local .dogcats/ is winning and deletes it — which also deletes their namespace and visibility config.

Two further gaps in the same list: _fallback_to_global_or_default tries the main worktree root's .dogcats/ before the global default_storage, and the walk stops at get_rc_walkup_boundary rather than the filesystem root as step 3 states.
acceptance: Steps 1 and 2 are collapsed into one rule (walk up from the cwd, cwd included, checking .dogcatrc then .dogcats/ at each level). The linked-worktree fallback is documented before the global-default step. The boundary is stated as get_rc_walkup_boundary, not the filesystem root.

description:
docs/web-ui.md:36 says 'dcat web propose binds 127.0.0.1 by default and has no authentication'. The default is actually os.environ.get(WEB_HOST_ENV_VAR) or WEB_DEFAULT_HOST (cli/_cmd_web.py:50-52), so an exported DCAT_WEB_HOST changes it with nothing on the command line to hint otherwise.

Cost: an operator with DCAT_WEB_HOST=0.0.0.0 in their shell profile reads that sentence as a guarantee and starts an unauthenticated issue-submission form on a public interface.

Six env vars are read by src/ and appear in zero .md files:
- DCAT_WEB_HOST, DCAT_WEB_PORT
- DCAT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECS, DCAT_GIT_TIMEOUT_SECS
- DCAT_UNSAFE_CROSS_USER, DCAT_RC_WALKUP_UNRESTRICTED

The last two disable security checks that docs/sharing-a-database.md:134 describes as unconditional, so that doc is also overstating its guarantees.

Unearned-certainty and machine-specific facts in four prose sites
description:
Four small rot risks, grouped because each is a one-line edit:

(a) pyproject.toml:149 — a trailing '(colophon-59t5)' citation. Every other id in this tree is dogcat-*, which dcat show resolves from the committed .dogcats/. This one belongs to a different repo's tracker and can never be resolved from here. The preceding sentence already carries the whole rationale including the importtime numbers, so the parenthetical is pure dead weight.

(b) docs/releasing.md:33-36 — 'On this machine it is checked out at ../personal/homebrew-tap/Formula/dogcat.rb; the sibling directory ../homebrew-tap is an unrelated tap.' False on every clone but one. The closing sentence ('the formula lives in a separate repo; confirm the path before editing') already carries the durable instruction.

(c) src/dogcat/utils.py:10 and src/dogcat/constants.py:40 — both claim the chars/4 estimator 'intentionally over-counts compared to real BPE tokenisation, so staying under a budget measured with this function guarantees the actual token footprint is even smaller'. Nothing calibrates len(text)//4 against a real tokenizer; tests/test_utils.py only pins the arithmetic, and its own test_unicode_counts_codepoints shows four accented chars counting as one token. The budget guards dcat prime, whose output is dense in box-drawing glyphs. 'Guarantees' is doing work no measurement did.

(d) tests/conftest.py:35 and docs/testing.md:13 — both hardcode 'failing 66 tests' / '66 failures'. The number changes with every test added or removed, and the two copies can drift apart independently.
acceptance: (a) parenthetical deleted. (b) machine-specific paths deleted, closing sentence kept. (c) both copies say the estimate is uncalibrated and counts codepoints, and describe MAX_PRIME_TOKENS as a tripwire rather than a bound. (d) the number is gone from both files.

Unknown-status merge rank differs between issues and proposals with no rationale at either site
description:
In the merge driver an unrecognised status falls back to rank 1 for issues (merge_driver.py:418) and rank 0 for proposals (merge_driver.py:452). Neither site says why the two differ, or why either number was chosen.

This is reachable, not theoretical: Status.UNKNOWN is a supported forward-compat sentinel, so a record written by a newer dcat lands here.

Cost: the asymmetry reads as an oversight, so a maintainer normalising the two flips merge outcomes for exactly the records that forward compatibility is meant to protect.

The plausible reading is that issues treat an unknown status as active (never beats a close or tombstone, never loses to a draft) while proposals treat it as open — but that is inference, not documentation.
acceptance: Both sites carry a comment stating what the fallback rank means for that record kind and why the two differ, or 'why unknown, ask the author' if the asymmetry turns out to be unintentional. No behaviour change.

Bare except Exception in the propose app has no note that the breadth is deliberate
description:
src/dogcat/web/propose/__init__.py:105 — a bare 'except Exception:' collapses namespace collection down to [resolved_namespace]. Nothing says why swallowing everything is the right call, and ruff's BLE001 is globally ignored in this repo so no linter flags it either.

Cost: the breadth looks like laziness, so a maintainer narrows it to (ValueError, RuntimeError). That turns a corrupt or unreadable store into a dcat web propose that will not boot, when the current behaviour degrades gracefully to a usable single-namespace form.
acceptance: The handler carries a comment stating the breadth is deliberate and what it protects: a corrupt or unreadable store must still yield a usable single-namespace form rather than failing startup. No behaviour change.

MAX_TITLE_LEN, MAX_DESC_LEN and MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN carry no provenance
description:
src/dogcat/constants.py:280 — MAX_TITLE_LEN = 500, MAX_DESC_LEN = 50_000 and MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN = 64 have no note on where the numbers came from. Every other limit in this file justifies its magnitude, so these three read as the odd ones out.

They are not decorative: they are enforced across four surfaces — validate_issue, the TUI save path, the web propose form, and the MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN * 4 pre-normalisation cap that derives from MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN. Nobody can tune one safely without knowing what it bounds.

'Chosen by feel, no measured basis' is an acceptable answer and better than silence — it tells the next reader the number is movable.
acceptance: Each of the three carries a line stating what it bounds and why that magnitude, or an explicit statement that it was chosen by feel. The derivation of the MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN * 4 pre-cap is stated at that site.

Deprecation deadline with no version, plus an unused pydantic dep in both PEP 723 script headers
description:
Two stale-marker problems:

(a) src/dogcat/config.py:784-786 — the *_prefix back-compat shims say 'keep the old names importable for one release for any out-of-tree callers; remove them the release after'. No version is named. The shims landed after v0.13.0 and shipped in v0.13.1, so the stated release has already elapsed, and the note carries no id that would surface the deadline at release time. Nothing in-tree imports them except tests/test_config.py, so they will ship indefinitely.

(b) dcat.py:6 and tabcomp.py:6 — both PEP 723 '# /// script' dependency blocks list 'pydantic'. The name appears in no source file and is absent from pyproject.toml, so every ./dcat.py and uv run ./tabcomp.py invocation — the forms AGENTS.md prescribes — resolves and installs it for nothing. The same blocks also disagree with pyproject on textual: dcat.py pins >=8.0.0, tabcomp.py is unpinned, pyproject says >=8.2.8.
acceptance: (a) The config.py note names a concrete removal version, or cites a tracked issue id. (b) 'pydantic' is gone from both script headers and the textual entries match pyproject's >=8.2.8. ./dcat.py still runs.

Docstring gaps on storage, idgen, serde and merge APIs that hide real footguns
description:
Six public-surface docstrings that exist but omit the fact a caller needs. Grouped because the fix is the same shape at each site: add the missing Returns:/Raises: content.

- src/dogcat/storage.py:744 and :758 — list() and get() hand out the LIVE Issue objects held in LazyIssueMap, whose own docstring guarantees identity. A caller mutating a returned issue silently changes in-memory store state without persisting it. list(None) also includes tombstoned and closed issues.
- src/dogcat/storage.py:1617 — archive() has no Args:/Returns:. ArchiveStats.issues is len(archivable_ids), the count REQUESTED, so it stays non-zero even when nothing was archived; dependencies and links are real counts. archive_path.parent is created as a side effect.
- src/dogcat/idgen.py:288, and the same at :272, :359, :399 — every generator registers the minted full id in self.existing_ids, so these are not pure functions: two calls with identical title and timestamp return different hashes. The length+2 and microsecond-nonce fallbacks return a hash LONGER than id_length.
- src/dogcat/models_serde.py:154 — no Raises: despite raising KeyError on missing title/created_at/updated_at/comment fields and ValueError from datetime.fromisoformat. That is precisely the failure set precheck_issue_record documents and promises to mirror, and LazyIssueMap assumes this converter cannot raise.
- src/dogcat/_jsonl_io.py:27 and :82 — both wrap OSError into RuntimeError, so a caller writing 'except OSError' around a save catches nothing.
- src/dogcat/merge_driver.py:131 — parse_conflicted_jsonl returns ([], [], []) when the input has no <<<<<<< marker, indistinguishable from 'conflicted but empty'. git_rebase depends on that sentinel via 'if not ours and not theirs: continue'.
acceptance: Each site documents the omitted fact: live-reference vs copy and the unfiltered list contents; the requested-vs-archived count and the mkdir; the existing_ids registration and the longer fallback hashes; the KeyError/ValueError set and the precheck cross-reference; Raises: RuntimeError wrapping OSError; the no-marker sentinel. No behaviour change.

feature_flags docstrings describe a per-member convention for an enum with no members
description:
src/dogcat/feature_flags.py:6 (module docstring) and :18-22 (class docstring) describe FeatureFlag as 'the single source of truth for all flags' and explain that 'each member's value is the suffix used in the env var name' — the DCAT_FEATURE_<VALUE> convention. The enum declares zero members, so feature_enabled is unreachable and dcat features always takes its empty branch.

CHANGELOG.md:27 / dogcat-15vs records the empty state as a deliberate decision, but neither docstring says so, so a reader has to open the enum body to learn the flags do not exist and then guess whether that is a bug.

This is not a duplicate of dogcat-15vs, which closed the dcat guide advertising and explicitly kept the empty state.
acceptance: The class docstring states that the enum is intentionally empty today and that this is where a flag gets registered, citing dogcat-15vs. The convention then reads as forward-looking rather than as describing members that exist.

Strip the 'Extracted from the god class' refactor preamble from ~20 docstrings
description:
The same refactor-provenance opener recurs across roughly twenty sites, spending one to three sentences on where the code used to live before saying what it does. 'Extracted from JSONLStorage so the god class shrinks toward cohesive units' appears verbatim in more than one file. Git blame already holds this, and 'the god class shrinks toward cohesive units' states nothing checkable — it dates the moment it stops being true.

Module-level sites: _records.py:5, _branch.py:5, _archive.py:3, _compaction.py:3, _indexes.py:3, _queries.py:3, _persistence.py:10, _jsonl_io.py:5, models_serde.py:3, git.py:3, status_display.py:6.

Member-level twins ('Replaces the N-line pattern', 'previously re-implemented at every call site'): storage.py:605, storage.py:713, inbox.py:264, inbox.py:283, cli/_helpers.py:162, cli/_helpers.py:644, web/propose/__init__.py:32, cli/_cmd_update.py:88, cli/_cmd_admin.py:43, cli/_cmd_chart.py:108.

Two of these are worse than merely redundant. cli/_helpers.py:644 says 'Replaces the older quartet (_is_priority_shorthand, _is_type_shorthand, _is_status_shorthand, _is_shorthand)' — those four names exist nowhere in the tree except that sentence, so a reader greps them and finds only the docstring that mentions them. cli/_cmd_chart.py:108 describes a return shape _chart_data no longer has, so a skimming reader takes away the wrong signature.

MUST NOT be touched by this sweep: merge_driver.py:31 and :386, where 'the rule used to be new_ts >= old_ts' warns a future editor off reintroducing a fixed bug. That is history doing real work.

Where a live fact rides alongside the provenance, the fact survives: _queries.py's 'can be tested directly against plain dicts', models_serde.py's import-cycle explanation, _archive.py's protocol/fake note, status_display.py's single-source-of-truth constraint.
acceptance: The provenance clause is gone from every listed site and each docstring opens with what the module or function IS. Frozen counts ('56 call sites', '~85-line rewrite body', 'five separate app.state writes') are gone. The merge_driver.py regression notes are untouched. just lint-all passes.

Collapse five clusters where the same rationale is restated three to five times
description:
Five places where one fact is argued repeatedly. In each case keep one canonical copy and replace the rest with a pointer.

1. src/dogcat/idgen.py:1-55 — a 55-line module docstring with two ASCII tables, three probability formulas and four paragraphs of derivation before the module's actual job. The formulas are then restated in collision_probability:159 and cumulative_collision_probability:178, which implement them. Keep the ID_LENGTH_THRESHOLDS table and the one load-bearing sentence: collisions affect retry rate, not correctness — each is detected against existing_ids and resolved by nonce or length+2. Move the birthday-paradox derivation to docs/ and point at dcat doctor --check-id-distribution for live figures.

2. src/dogcat/_schema.py:1-62 — a 62-line four-section design doc for a module holding four small functions, ending in a 3-step procedure for SCHEMA_BREAKING_THRESHOLD which the same paragraph admits is unused. Keep two facts: dcat_version is the tool version that wrote the record, not a separate schema number; only MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH is compared. Cut the procedure to one line at the constant itself.

3. src/dogcat/merge_driver.py — the status-finality rationale appears in full four times (module docstring:19-38, _ISSUE_STATUS_RANK:306-311, _merge_issues_lww:402-408, _merge_proposals:436-442) and is summarised a fifth at :526-527. Keep the module docstring (docs/merge-coverage.md names it canonical) and the _ISSUE_STATUS_RANK comment, which sits on the data. Cut both function docstrings to one line referring up.

4. src/dogcat/merge_driver.py:384-393 — _tie_break_key re-derives the whole dogcat-1xgi scenario already spelled out at :30-34, told again in docs/merge-coverage.md:21 and a fourth time in tests/test_merge_driver.py:304-309. Keep only the two facts true just here: ordering is arbitrary and only its stability matters; full_id cannot serve because it is equal on both sides by construction.

5. src/dogcat/cli/_helpers.py — the eval_str rationale is explained three times in one file (:50-56, :116-122, :143-149). The first copy even says 'the same reason _make_alias below does it' and then re-explains it anyway. Keep the with_ns_shim copy as canonical; replace the other two with a pointer.

Also docs/merge-coverage.md:21 and :82 — two Status cells holding 75-word and 55-word essays in a column whose declared vocabulary is green/partial/gap. Set both to green and move the narrative to a History subsection or a numbered footnote.
acceptance: Each cluster has exactly one canonical statement and pointers elsewhere. No fact is lost. The merge-coverage Status column contains only green/partial/gap values. just lint-all and just test-all pass.

Also docs/merge-coverage.md:21 and :82 — two Status cells holding 75-word and 55-word essays in a column whose declared vocabulary is green/partial/gap. Set both to green and move the narrative to a History subsection or a numbered footnote.

description:

- 96 '# ---...---' divider lines (48 blocks) across 14 test files, each sitting directly on top of the class it names — '# Unit tests for validate_issue' above 'class TestValidateIssue:' whose docstring already says 'Test individual issue record validation'. - src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py:156, 171, 186, 199, 217 — '# Check 1:' through '# Check 5:' duplicate the HealthCheck description= string three to eight lines below, and inserting a check means hand-renumbering with nothing failing if you do not.
- src/dogcat/cli/_validate.py:167, 177, 187, 198, 377, 389 — '# Required fields', '# Status validation', '# Issue type validation', '# Priority validation' restate the constant names beneath them.
- src/dogcat/cli/_validate.py:476, src/dogcat/constants.py:20, src/dogcat/config.py:32, src/dogcat/storage.py:525, src/dogcat/inbox.py:213 — lone section markers echoing the names that follow.

Comments and docstrings restating the code:
- src/dogcat/idgen.py:313, 317, 325; src/dogcat/tui/dashboard.py:202, 229, 251, 384, 408, 418, 512; src/dogcat/storage.py:231, 236; src/dogcat/inbox.py:73; src/dogcat/models.py:243; src/dogcat/deps.py:49, 120, 158, 221, 245 ('storage: The storage instance' five times).
- src/dogcat/web/propose/routes.py:60 — _is_valid_namespace copies the first line of constants.is_valid_namespace's docstring while dropping the part that mattered: the ASCII whitelist, the 1-64 cap, and the NFKC-before-calling contract. Replace with why the alias exists plus a pointer to the canonical.

Constraint: pyproject.toml enables ruff's full D family, so a public docstring cannot be deleted. For docstring rows replace the echo with the missing constraint — models.py's enum one-liners should say that UNKNOWN is a forward-compat sentinel and that a tombstone is not 'closed'; storage.py:1689/1694 should say all_dependencies/all_links return a copy; config.py:173/185 should say whether the returned path exists. models.py:593 (LinkType) is the counter-example done right — copy its shape.

MUST NOT be touched: idgen.py's '36**2 = 1296x keyspace' and 'Last resort' notes; models.py's PEP 562 paragraph; dashboard.py's '# Narrow mode: push modal editor' and the 'recompose() is async' comment; storage.py's _bad_lines and memoization comments; deps.py's detect_cycles RecursionError note and _BLOCKING_STATUSES rationale; constants.py's DEFAULT_NAMESPACE, SPLIT_PANE_MIN_*, GITATTRIBUTES_ENTRY, STATUS_VALUES_HELP and MAX_PRIME_TOKENS comments; storage.py's mixin-provenance comment (delete only the '# Event emission helpers' label above it).

Also in scope, from the llm-slop lens: src/dogcat/storage.py:191 has a stray leading comma from a bad rewrap ('# , so ID-targeted commands don't construct the whole') — rewrap those three lines.

title: Delete decorative dividers, ordinal labels and code-restating comments repo-wide
Comment Cop sweep: fix misleading, rotting, and redundant prose across the codebase
description:
Umbrella for the findings of a Comment Cop review run on 2026-08-09 against branch docs260809 (commit a75488f). Ten reviewer lenses (contradicts-code, rambling, transient, restates-code, missing-why, dead-comments, docstring-gaps, doc-drift, noise, llm-slop) analysed a 581KB prose-dense snapshot of src/dogcat, docs/, README.md, AGENTS.md, the web assets, and a sample of tests. Findings were deduplicated and ranked by a distillation pass.

Scope is the documentation layer only: comments, docstrings, and prose docs. No child issue here asks for a behaviour change. Where a docstring is wrong because the code has a real gap (see the child on models.py strip_control_chars), the fix is to state the truth in the prose; any code change is a separate issue.

Children are grouped by tier:
- Red (priority 1): prose that misleads a maintainer into a bug or misstates a safety-critical property.
- Yellow (priority 2): docstrings contradicting code, doc drift, rot-prone anecdotes, API docstring gaps.
- Green (priority 3): rambling, restatements, decorative noise.

Two constraints that apply to every child:
1. pyproject.toml enables ruff's full D (pydocstyle) family, so a public docstring cannot simply be deleted without failing just lint. For docstring findings the action is replace-the-echo-with-the-missing-fact, never delete.
2. AGENTS.md declares src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_example_md.py, src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py and README.md deliberate near-duplicate product surface. Changing one means checking the other two.

Acceptance: every child closed or explicitly deferred, and just lint-all plus just test-all pass.

title: Comment Cop sweep: fix misleading, rotting, and redundant prose across the codebase
Merge-driver prose claims git falls back to its default merge on exit 1 — it does not
description:
Three sites say the merge driver exits 1 'so git falls back to its default merge strategy'. That is false. Git treats a non-zero merge-driver exit as a conflict on that path: it leaves the ours-side file (%A) exactly as it was and marks the path conflicted. No fallback merge runs. AGENTS.md already documents the real behaviour ('the file holds ours-side content only — staging it discards the other branch's issues'), so the source contradicts the repo's own guardrail doc.

Cost: the log message at _cmd_docs.py:481 is what a user sees at the exact moment the driver fails. It reassures them that git handled it, so they stage the file and silently drop every issue from the other branch.

Sites:
- src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py:444 — command docstring
- src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py:481 — user-facing log line
- tests/test_merge_driver.py:766 — test docstring ('exits 1 so git falls back'), which is what a maintainer reads when deciding the exit code is safe
acceptance: All three sites state that git marks the path conflicted and keeps ours-side content. The word 'falls back' appears at none of them. The log line warns against staging the file blindly. No behaviour change: the driver still exits 1.

title: Merge-driver prose claims git falls back to its default merge on exit 1 — it does not
Document why InboxStorage._append has no should_compact check — copying the sibling would erase the inbox event log
description:
JSONLStorage._append runs a should_compact() check that can trigger a full rewrite. InboxStorage._append does not, and that omission is load-bearing: InboxStorage._save_locked serializes only proposal records, so any rewrite of inbox.jsonl drops every event record the shared emitter appended. JSONLStorage._save_locked preserves events via compact_snapshot, so the parallel class names read as an accidental inconsistency rather than a deliberate divergence.

Cost: a maintainer restoring parity between the two _append methods destroys inbox history, and nothing in the file warns them. The fact currently lives only in docs/web-ui.md, which nobody reads while editing inbox.py.

Sites:
- src/dogcat/inbox.py:189 (_append) — needs the do-not-add-compaction warning
- src/dogcat/inbox.py:166/171 (_save / _save_locked) — needs the proposals-only rewrite statement and the explicit contrast with JSONLStorage._save_locked
acceptance: inbox.py states at both sites that the rewrite is proposals-only, that it therefore drops event records, that this diverges from JSONLStorage._save_locked on purpose, and that _append must not gain a should_compact branch. No behaviour change.

title: Document why InboxStorage._append has no should_compact check — copying the sibling would erase the inbox event log
strip_control_chars docstring claims a guarantee the close/delete paths do not honour
description:
src/dogcat/models.py:509 says the helper is 'used by validate_issue/validate_proposal so the storage layer can never persist a record carrying \x1b[2J'. The strip runs on the create() and update() paths only. JSONLStorage.close() (storage.py:1147) and delete() (storage.py:1255) assign closed_reason / deleted_reason and append the record with no validate_issue call, so a reason string containing a terminal escape is written verbatim to issues.jsonl. Records arriving via merge or compaction are not re-validated either.

The very next docstring in the file (sanitize_for_terminal) already concedes the hole with 'even if a record predates the validate-time strip', so the two docstrings contradict each other.

Scope note: this issue is the prose fix only. Whether close()/delete() should also strip is a behaviour question — file it separately if wanted.

Site: src/dogcat/models.py:509
acceptance: The docstring names the covered paths (create, update) instead of asserting an absolute, states that close/delete reasons and merge/compaction-arriving records are not re-validated, and directs callers to render through sanitize_for_terminal. No behaviour change in this issue.

title: strip_control_chars docstring claims a guarantee the close/delete paths do not honour
_resolve_dogcats_path docstring claims parity with the hardened walk-up it does not implement
description:
src/dogcat/config.py:611 — _resolve_dogcats_path walks up from the cwd looking for a .dogcatrc and accepts the first one it finds. Its docstring says it 'mirrors the walk-up logic in cli._helpers.find_dogcats_dir'. It does not. The real walk-up applies get_rc_walkup_boundary and refuse_if_rc_target_cross_user; this copy is unbounded to the filesystem root, applies no cross-user refusal, and swallows a malformed rc with 'except ValueError: pass'. Both sibling walk-ups (_find_rc_parent in this same file, walkup_find_store in cli/_helpers.py) carry explicit rationale for those guards.

Cost: the word 'mirrors' tells a reader the hardening is present. It is not, so a planted /tmp/.dogcatrc can steer namespace resolution through this path without hitting the defense the other path enforces.

Scope note: prose only. If the missing guards are a real defect rather than a deliberate exemption, that is a separate issue — this one just makes the docstring tell the truth.
acceptance: The docstring no longer claims parity. It states that this walk is unbounded and applies no cross-user refusal, unlike _find_rc_parent and walkup_find_store, and either gives the reason it is safe here or says the rationale is unknown. No behaviour change.

title: _resolve_dogcats_path docstring claims parity with the hardened walk-up it does not implement
Explain the or-not-and archive filter in storage.py before someone 'fixes' it
description:
src/dogcat/storage.py:1674 and :1680 filter in-memory dependencies and links after an archive rewrite with:

    if dep.issue_id not in archived_ids or dep.depends_on_id not in archived_ids

The 'or' reads like an 'and' typo. It is not: it is the De Morgan inverse of classify_archived_line's rule that an edge is archived only when BOTH endpoints are archived. A half-archived edge stays in issues.jsonl, so it must stay in memory too.

Cost: changing it to 'and' drops in-memory edges whose surviving endpoint is still live, desyncing memory from the file that was just rewritten. Nothing at either call site records the constraint, so the 'fix' looks obviously correct.

Sites: src/dogcat/storage.py:1674, :1680
acceptance: Both sites carry a comment stating that 'or' is deliberate, that it mirrors classify_archived_line's both-endpoints rule, and what breaks if it becomes 'and'. No behaviour change.

title: Explain the or-not-and archive filter in storage.py before someone 'fixes' it
with_ns_shim docstring describes a global-callback mechanism that does not exist
description:
src/dogcat/cli/_helpers.py:43 — the 'why' paragraph on with_ns_shim says the --namespace / --all-namespaces flags are 'owned by the global Typer callback' and that 'the actual filter is applied by get_namespace_filter() reading the process state set by the global callback'.

None of that is true. The global callback in cli/__init__.py declares only --json and -C/--repo. No namespace process state exists. get_namespace_filter() reads config plus an explicit argument. The shim kwargs.pop()s both values and discards them, so 'dcat close ID --namespace ns' parses fine and filters nothing.

What the shim actually buys: the command parses the options without error, and _ns_filter_from_ctx (cli/_completions.py:20) can read them off the Click context during tab completion.

Cost: a reader debugging why --namespace has no effect on a mutation command is sent to a callback that never touches namespaces.
acceptance: The docstring states the real reason the options are declared (parse compatibility plus completion via ctx.params), names _ns_filter_from_ctx as the consumer, and says plainly that the runtime command ignores the values. No behaviour change.

title: with_ns_shim docstring describes a global-callback mechanism that does not exist
close() docstring tells the reader to run dcat reopen on a tombstone, which reopen rejects
description:
src/dogcat/storage.py:1165 — the close() docstring says a tombstoned issue 'cannot be closed; use dcat reopen first'. reopen() (storage.py:1232) raises ValueError for any status other than CLOSED, so that instruction cannot succeed. close()'s own raised error already says the opposite and correct thing: 'A tombstone is permanent; no command restores it.'

So one method carries two contradictory statements about tombstones, and the wrong one is the one a reader hits first.
acceptance: The 'use dcat reopen first' clause is gone and the docstring states that a tombstone is terminal, matching the error text the method already raises. No behaviour change.

title: close() docstring tells the reader to run dcat reopen on a tombstone, which reopen rejects
Four docstrings name a 'dcat admin' command group that does not exist
description:
_cmd_admin.register() puts export and repair-jsonl directly on the top-level app; there is no 'admin' sub-command group. Four docstrings still spell the old prefix, so a reader copying them out gets 'No such command'. Every dcat doctor hint already says the correct top-level form, so the file set is internally inconsistent.

Sites:
- src/dogcat/models.py:189 — Dependency.to_export_dict, 'dcat admin export'
- src/dogcat/models.py:218 — Link.to_export_dict, 'dcat admin export'
- src/dogcat/storage.py:227 — _bad_lines comment, 'dcat admin repair-jsonl'
- src/dogcat/storage.py:251 — _bad_lines comment, 'dcat admin repair-jsonl'
acceptance: All four read 'dcat export' / 'dcat repair-jsonl'. A repo-wide grep for 'dcat admin' returns nothing outside git history.

title: Four docstrings name a 'dcat admin' command group that does not exist
Two hand-rolled atomic writes skip atomic_rewrite_jsonl's mode preservation with no note saying why
description:
_jsonl_io.atomic_rewrite_jsonl documents mode preservation as load-bearing: without it 'a shared .dogcats becomes inaccessible to everyone except the writer after the first compaction'. Two write paths reimplement tempfile-write + replace() inline and omit that step, with no comment recording whether the omission was considered:

- src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py:399 — dcat git rebase
- src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py:467 — the merge-driver command

Cost: on a shared store (see docs/sharing-a-database.md) either path can leave issues.jsonl readable only by the last writer, and the helper that knows this is one import away.

Scope note: prose only. Routing these through atomic_rewrite_jsonl would be a behaviour change — file it separately if that is the preferred fix.
acceptance: Both sites carry a comment saying they do not use atomic_rewrite_jsonl, what that skips (mode preservation), and either the reason it is safe here or that the reason is unknown.

title: Two hand-rolled atomic writes skip atomic_rewrite_jsonl's mode preservation with no note saying why
merge_jsonl's Returns section omits that unrecognised record types are dropped from the output
description:
src/dogcat/merge_driver.py:519 — the merge_jsonl docstring enumerates the four record kinds it merges but never says what happens to anything else. A record whose classify_record() result is 'unknown' — for example a record_type written by a newer dcat — does not appear in the returned list at all.

Both callers (dcat git merge-driver and dcat git rebase) write the returned list over the file verbatim. So for a caller, 'dropped from the result' means 'erased from the store', and the docstring gives no hint that forward-compat records are at risk.

The assembly order of the returned list (issues, proposals, deps, links, then events sorted by timestamp) is also undocumented even though the list IS the file content.
acceptance: Returns: states that only issue, proposal, event, dependency and link records survive, that any other record_type is dropped, that callers overwriting the file therefore erase it, and documents the assembly order. No behaviour change.

title: merge_jsonl's Returns section omits that unrecognised record types are dropped from the output
CLI root callback has no docstring for its three process-wide side effects
description:
src/dogcat/cli/__init__.py:21 — the Typer root callback is the entry point for every dcat invocation and has no docstring. The leading underscore exempts it from ruff's D103, so lint never asked for one.

Three undocumented behaviours, all process-wide:
1. -C/--repo resolves the path strictly and calls os.chdir() on the process before any subcommand runs, exiting 1 if the path is missing or not a directory.
2. --json resets and sets module-global JSON state that every command reads via is_json().
3. A bare 'dcat' with no subcommand prints help and exits 0.

Cost: anyone adding a command or writing a test against the CLI has to read the body to learn that the process cwd moves under them.
acceptance: The callback carries a docstring covering all three behaviours, naming os.chdir() and the global JSON state explicitly. No behaviour change.

title: CLI root callback has no docstring for its three process-wide side effects
UpdateRequest docstring says its fields mirror UPDATABLE_FIELDS; seven fields are missing
description:
src/dogcat/models.py:414 — the UpdateRequest docstring says 'Field names mirror JSONLStorage.UPDATABLE_FIELDS'. UpdateRequest has 17 fields; UPDATABLE_FIELDS has 24. The seven absent ones are closed_at, closed_by, deleted_at, deleted_by, deleted_reason, original_type and comments.

Cost: 'mirror' tells a caller the typed path can set anything the storage layer accepts. It cannot — those seven are reachable only through the plain-dict path, and a caller who trusts the docstring will not go looking for why their update silently did nothing.
acceptance: The docstring says 'are a subset of' rather than 'mirror' and names the seven fields that only the plain-dict path can set. No behaviour change.

title: UpdateRequest docstring says its fields mirror UPDATABLE_FIELDS; seven fields are missing
Unknown-status merge rank differs between issues and proposals with no rationale at either site
description:
In the merge driver an unrecognised status falls back to rank 1 for issues (merge_driver.py:418) and rank 0 for proposals (merge_driver.py:452). Neither site says why the two differ, or why either number was chosen.

This is reachable, not theoretical: Status.UNKNOWN is a supported forward-compat sentinel, so a record written by a newer dcat lands here.

Cost: the asymmetry reads as an oversight, so a maintainer normalising the two flips merge outcomes for exactly the records that forward compatibility is meant to protect.

The plausible reading is that issues treat an unknown status as active (never beats a close or tombstone, never loses to a draft) while proposals treat it as open — but that is inference, not documentation.
acceptance: Both sites carry a comment stating what the fallback rank means for that record kind and why the two differ, or 'why unknown, ask the author' if the asymmetry turns out to be unintentional. No behaviour change.

title: Unknown-status merge rank differs between issues and proposals with no rationale at either site
Five file:line citations in docs and tests point at the wrong lines
description:
Line-number citations in prose rot on the first edit above the cited line. Five are already wrong, and three reviewer lenses caught them independently:

- docs/web-ui.md:25 — cites constants.py:291 for the CSP string; WEB_CSP_HEADER is at constants.py:305, and 291 lands inside an unrelated declaration.
- docs/cli-conventions.md:17 — cites _cmd_config.py:39 for _KNOWN_KEYS; it is at :42, and 39 is the closing brace of _ARRAY_KEYS, so a reader edits the wrong constant.
- docs/cli-conventions.md:50 — cites _cmd_chart.py:146 for _complete_by_values; defined at :150.
- docs/merge-coverage.md:28 — cites merge_driver.py:309-318 for _ISSUE_STATUS_RANK; the dict spans 311-320, so the cited range starts mid-comment and cuts off 'tombstone' — the highest rank, which is exactly what that row's finality argument rests on.
- tests/test_merge_driver.py:352 — same wrong 309-318 range.

Preferred fix is to drop the numbers entirely and cite the symbol name, which is grep-able and cannot rot. Note that four further citations elsewhere in these docs are currently correct; converting all of them to symbol names in the same pass stops the whole class of finding recurring.
acceptance: No wrong line citation remains. Either the five ranges are corrected or, preferably, the file:line form is replaced by symbol names throughout the docs set.

title: Five file:line citations in docs and tests point at the wrong lines
Store-resolution order in docs/sharing-a-database.md contradicts walkup_find_store and omits the worktree step
description:
docs/sharing-a-database.md:133 numbers the resolution order as: step 1 'Local .dogcats/ in the current directory', step 2 walk up checking .dogcatrc then .dogcats/ 'at each ancestor directory', step 3 fall back to the global default.

The real loop (walkup_find_store, cli/_helpers.py:282-304) checks .dogcatrc before .dogcats/ at EVERY level including the cwd — one pass, cwd treated no differently from an ancestor. get_storage even carries a comment saying exactly this: 'Always resolve via find_dogcats_dir() to respect .dogcatrc priority over a local .dogcats/ directory (which may only contain config.local.toml)'. So step 1 contradicts step 2, and contradicts this doc's own example layout where every app repo holds both a .dogcatrc and a .dogcats/config.local.toml.

Cost: a reader debugging 'why isn't my repo using the shared store?' concludes from step 1 that the local .dogcats/ is winning and deletes it — which also deletes their namespace and visibility config.

Two further gaps in the same list: _fallback_to_global_or_default tries the main worktree root's .dogcats/ before the global default_storage, and the walk stops at get_rc_walkup_boundary rather than the filesystem root as step 3 states.
acceptance: Steps 1 and 2 are collapsed into one rule (walk up from the cwd, cwd included, checking .dogcatrc then .dogcats/ at each level). The linked-worktree fallback is documented before the global-default step. The boundary is stated as get_rc_walkup_boundary, not the filesystem root.

title: Store-resolution order in docs/sharing-a-database.md contradicts walkup_find_store and omits the worktree step
docs/web-ui.md states a bind address six undocumented env vars can override
description:
docs/web-ui.md:36 says 'dcat web propose binds 127.0.0.1 by default and has no authentication'. The default is actually os.environ.get(WEB_HOST_ENV_VAR) or WEB_DEFAULT_HOST (cli/_cmd_web.py:50-52), so an exported DCAT_WEB_HOST changes it with nothing on the command line to hint otherwise.

Cost: an operator with DCAT_WEB_HOST=0.0.0.0 in their shell profile reads that sentence as a guarantee and starts an unauthenticated issue-submission form on a public interface.

Six env vars are read by src/ and appear in zero .md files:
- DCAT_WEB_HOST, DCAT_WEB_PORT
- DCAT_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SECS, DCAT_GIT_TIMEOUT_SECS
- DCAT_UNSAFE_CROSS_USER, DCAT_RC_WALKUP_UNRESTRICTED

The last two disable security checks that docs/sharing-a-database.md:134 describes as unconditional, so that doc is also overstating its guarantees.
acceptance: docs/web-ui.md:36 reads 'binds 127.0.0.1 unless DCAT_WEB_HOST overrides it'. An env-var table covers the web pair in docs/web-ui.md and the two override switches in docs/sharing-a-database.md, marked as escape hatches. The unconditional phrasing in sharing-a-database.md is qualified.

title: docs/web-ui.md states a bind address six undocumented env vars can override
Unearned-certainty and machine-specific facts in four prose sites
description:
Four small rot risks, grouped because each is a one-line edit:

(a) pyproject.toml:149 — a trailing '(colophon-59t5)' citation. Every other id in this tree is dogcat-*, which dcat show resolves from the committed .dogcats/. This one belongs to a different repo's tracker and can never be resolved from here. The preceding sentence already carries the whole rationale including the importtime numbers, so the parenthetical is pure dead weight.

(b) docs/releasing.md:33-36 — 'On this machine it is checked out at ../personal/homebrew-tap/Formula/dogcat.rb; the sibling directory ../homebrew-tap is an unrelated tap.' False on every clone but one. The closing sentence ('the formula lives in a separate repo; confirm the path before editing') already carries the durable instruction.

(c) src/dogcat/utils.py:10 and src/dogcat/constants.py:40 — both claim the chars/4 estimator 'intentionally over-counts compared to real BPE tokenisation, so staying under a budget measured with this function guarantees the actual token footprint is even smaller'. Nothing calibrates len(text)//4 against a real tokenizer; tests/test_utils.py only pins the arithmetic, and its own test_unicode_counts_codepoints shows four accented chars counting as one token. The budget guards dcat prime, whose output is dense in box-drawing glyphs. 'Guarantees' is doing work no measurement did.

(d) tests/conftest.py:35 and docs/testing.md:13 — both hardcode 'failing 66 tests' / '66 failures'. The number changes with every test added or removed, and the two copies can drift apart independently.
acceptance: (a) parenthetical deleted. (b) machine-specific paths deleted, closing sentence kept. (c) both copies say the estimate is uncalibrated and counts codepoints, and describe MAX_PRIME_TOKENS as a tripwire rather than a bound. (d) the number is gone from both files.

title: Unearned-certainty and machine-specific facts in four prose sites
Bare except Exception in the propose app has no note that the breadth is deliberate
description:
src/dogcat/web/propose/__init__.py:105 — a bare 'except Exception:' collapses namespace collection down to [resolved_namespace]. Nothing says why swallowing everything is the right call, and ruff's BLE001 is globally ignored in this repo so no linter flags it either.

Cost: the breadth looks like laziness, so a maintainer narrows it to (ValueError, RuntimeError). That turns a corrupt or unreadable store into a dcat web propose that will not boot, when the current behaviour degrades gracefully to a usable single-namespace form.
acceptance: The handler carries a comment stating the breadth is deliberate and what it protects: a corrupt or unreadable store must still yield a usable single-namespace form rather than failing startup. No behaviour change.

title: Bare except Exception in the propose app has no note that the breadth is deliberate
MAX_TITLE_LEN, MAX_DESC_LEN and MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN carry no provenance
description:
src/dogcat/constants.py:280 — MAX_TITLE_LEN = 500, MAX_DESC_LEN = 50_000 and MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN = 64 have no note on where the numbers came from. Every other limit in this file justifies its magnitude, so these three read as the odd ones out.

They are not decorative: they are enforced across four surfaces — validate_issue, the TUI save path, the web propose form, and the MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN * 4 pre-normalisation cap that derives from MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN. Nobody can tune one safely without knowing what it bounds.

'Chosen by feel, no measured basis' is an acceptable answer and better than silence — it tells the next reader the number is movable.
acceptance: Each of the three carries a line stating what it bounds and why that magnitude, or an explicit statement that it was chosen by feel. The derivation of the MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN * 4 pre-cap is stated at that site.

title: MAX_TITLE_LEN, MAX_DESC_LEN and MAX_NAMESPACE_LEN carry no provenance
Deprecation deadline with no version, plus an unused pydantic dep in both PEP 723 script headers
description:
Two stale-marker problems:

(a) src/dogcat/config.py:784-786 — the *_prefix back-compat shims say 'keep the old names importable for one release for any out-of-tree callers; remove them the release after'. No version is named. The shims landed after v0.13.0 and shipped in v0.13.1, so the stated release has already elapsed, and the note carries no id that would surface the deadline at release time. Nothing in-tree imports them except tests/test_config.py, so they will ship indefinitely.

(b) dcat.py:6 and tabcomp.py:6 — both PEP 723 '# /// script' dependency blocks list 'pydantic'. The name appears in no source file and is absent from pyproject.toml, so every ./dcat.py and uv run ./tabcomp.py invocation — the forms AGENTS.md prescribes — resolves and installs it for nothing. The same blocks also disagree with pyproject on textual: dcat.py pins >=8.0.0, tabcomp.py is unpinned, pyproject says >=8.2.8.
acceptance: (a) The config.py note names a concrete removal version, or cites a tracked issue id. (b) 'pydantic' is gone from both script headers and the textual entries match pyproject's >=8.2.8. ./dcat.py still runs.

title: Deprecation deadline with no version, plus an unused pydantic dep in both PEP 723 script headers
feature_flags docstrings describe a per-member convention for an enum with no members
description:
src/dogcat/feature_flags.py:6 (module docstring) and :18-22 (class docstring) describe FeatureFlag as 'the single source of truth for all flags' and explain that 'each member's value is the suffix used in the env var name' — the DCAT_FEATURE_<VALUE> convention. The enum declares zero members, so feature_enabled is unreachable and dcat features always takes its empty branch.

CHANGELOG.md:27 / dogcat-15vs records the empty state as a deliberate decision, but neither docstring says so, so a reader has to open the enum body to learn the flags do not exist and then guess whether that is a bug.

This is not a duplicate of dogcat-15vs, which closed the dcat guide advertising and explicitly kept the empty state.
acceptance: The class docstring states that the enum is intentionally empty today and that this is where a flag gets registered, citing dogcat-15vs. The convention then reads as forward-looking rather than as describing members that exist.

title: feature_flags docstrings describe a per-member convention for an enum with no members
Docstring gaps on storage, idgen, serde and merge APIs that hide real footguns
description:
Six public-surface docstrings that exist but omit the fact a caller needs. Grouped because the fix is the same shape at each site: add the missing Returns:/Raises: content.

- src/dogcat/storage.py:744 and :758 — list() and get() hand out the LIVE Issue objects held in LazyIssueMap, whose own docstring guarantees identity. A caller mutating a returned issue silently changes in-memory store state without persisting it. list(None) also includes tombstoned and closed issues.
- src/dogcat/storage.py:1617 — archive() has no Args:/Returns:. ArchiveStats.issues is len(archivable_ids), the count REQUESTED, so it stays non-zero even when nothing was archived; dependencies and links are real counts. archive_path.parent is created as a side effect.
- src/dogcat/idgen.py:288, and the same at :272, :359, :399 — every generator registers the minted full id in self.existing_ids, so these are not pure functions: two calls with identical title and timestamp return different hashes. The length+2 and microsecond-nonce fallbacks return a hash LONGER than id_length.
- src/dogcat/models_serde.py:154 — no Raises: despite raising KeyError on missing title/created_at/updated_at/comment fields and ValueError from datetime.fromisoformat. That is precisely the failure set precheck_issue_record documents and promises to mirror, and LazyIssueMap assumes this converter cannot raise.
- src/dogcat/_jsonl_io.py:27 and :82 — both wrap OSError into RuntimeError, so a caller writing 'except OSError' around a save catches nothing.
- src/dogcat/merge_driver.py:131 — parse_conflicted_jsonl returns ([], [], []) when the input has no <<<<<<< marker, indistinguishable from 'conflicted but empty'. git_rebase depends on that sentinel via 'if not ours and not theirs: continue'.
acceptance: Each site documents the omitted fact: live-reference vs copy and the unfiltered list contents; the requested-vs-archived count and the mkdir; the existing_ids registration and the longer fallback hashes; the KeyError/ValueError set and the precheck cross-reference; Raises: RuntimeError wrapping OSError; the no-marker sentinel. No behaviour change.

title: Docstring gaps on storage, idgen, serde and merge APIs that hide real footguns
Strip the 'Extracted from the god class' refactor preamble from ~20 docstrings
description:
The same refactor-provenance opener recurs across roughly twenty sites, spending one to three sentences on where the code used to live before saying what it does. 'Extracted from JSONLStorage so the god class shrinks toward cohesive units' appears verbatim in more than one file. Git blame already holds this, and 'the god class shrinks toward cohesive units' states nothing checkable — it dates the moment it stops being true.

Module-level sites: _records.py:5, _branch.py:5, _archive.py:3, _compaction.py:3, _indexes.py:3, _queries.py:3, _persistence.py:10, _jsonl_io.py:5, models_serde.py:3, git.py:3, status_display.py:6.

Member-level twins ('Replaces the N-line pattern', 'previously re-implemented at every call site'): storage.py:605, storage.py:713, inbox.py:264, inbox.py:283, cli/_helpers.py:162, cli/_helpers.py:644, web/propose/__init__.py:32, cli/_cmd_update.py:88, cli/_cmd_admin.py:43, cli/_cmd_chart.py:108.

Two of these are worse than merely redundant. cli/_helpers.py:644 says 'Replaces the older quartet (_is_priority_shorthand, _is_type_shorthand, _is_status_shorthand, _is_shorthand)' — those four names exist nowhere in the tree except that sentence, so a reader greps them and finds only the docstring that mentions them. cli/_cmd_chart.py:108 describes a return shape _chart_data no longer has, so a skimming reader takes away the wrong signature.

MUST NOT be touched by this sweep: merge_driver.py:31 and :386, where 'the rule used to be new_ts >= old_ts' warns a future editor off reintroducing a fixed bug. That is history doing real work.

Where a live fact rides alongside the provenance, the fact survives: _queries.py's 'can be tested directly against plain dicts', models_serde.py's import-cycle explanation, _archive.py's protocol/fake note, status_display.py's single-source-of-truth constraint.
acceptance: The provenance clause is gone from every listed site and each docstring opens with what the module or function IS. Frozen counts ('56 call sites', '~85-line rewrite body', 'five separate app.state writes') are gone. The merge_driver.py regression notes are untouched. just lint-all passes.

title: Strip the 'Extracted from the god class' refactor preamble from ~20 docstrings
Collapse five clusters where the same rationale is restated three to five times
description:
Five places where one fact is argued repeatedly. In each case keep one canonical copy and replace the rest with a pointer.

1. src/dogcat/idgen.py:1-55 — a 55-line module docstring with two ASCII tables, three probability formulas and four paragraphs of derivation before the module's actual job. The formulas are then restated in collision_probability:159 and cumulative_collision_probability:178, which implement them. Keep the ID_LENGTH_THRESHOLDS table and the one load-bearing sentence: collisions affect retry rate, not correctness — each is detected against existing_ids and resolved by nonce or length+2. Move the birthday-paradox derivation to docs/ and point at dcat doctor --check-id-distribution for live figures.

2. src/dogcat/_schema.py:1-62 — a 62-line four-section design doc for a module holding four small functions, ending in a 3-step procedure for SCHEMA_BREAKING_THRESHOLD which the same paragraph admits is unused. Keep two facts: dcat_version is the tool version that wrote the record, not a separate schema number; only MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH is compared. Cut the procedure to one line at the constant itself.

3. src/dogcat/merge_driver.py — the status-finality rationale appears in full four times (module docstring:19-38, _ISSUE_STATUS_RANK:306-311, _merge_issues_lww:402-408, _merge_proposals:436-442) and is summarised a fifth at :526-527. Keep the module docstring (docs/merge-coverage.md names it canonical) and the _ISSUE_STATUS_RANK comment, which sits on the data. Cut both function docstrings to one line referring up.

4. src/dogcat/merge_driver.py:384-393 — _tie_break_key re-derives the whole dogcat-1xgi scenario already spelled out at :30-34, told again in docs/merge-coverage.md:21 and a fourth time in tests/test_merge_driver.py:304-309. Keep only the two facts true just here: ordering is arbitrary and only its stability matters; full_id cannot serve because it is equal on both sides by construction.

5. src/dogcat/cli/_helpers.py — the eval_str rationale is explained three times in one file (:50-56, :116-122, :143-149). The first copy even says 'the same reason _make_alias below does it' and then re-explains it anyway. Keep the with_ns_shim copy as canonical; replace the other two with a pointer.

Also docs/merge-coverage.md:21 and :82 — two Status cells holding 75-word and 55-word essays in a column whose declared vocabulary is green/partial/gap. Set both to green and move the narrative to a History subsection or a numbered footnote.
acceptance: Each cluster has exactly one canonical statement and pointers elsewhere. No fact is lost. The merge-coverage Status column contains only green/partial/gap values. just lint-all and just test-all pass.

title: Collapse five clusters where the same rationale is restated three to five times
Delete decorative dividers, ordinal labels and code-restating comments repo-wide
description:
Comments and docstrings that carry no fact the code does not already show. Grouped because they are one mechanical sweep.

Dividers and banners:
- src/dogcat/demo.py — 11 '# ===...===' banner blocks (22 lines at 144/146, 482/484, 664/666, 869/871, 936/938, 1040/1042, 1085/1087, 1184/1186, 1251/1253, 1289/1291, 1305/1307) carve the single ~1330-line generate_demo_issues body into 'Epic 1', 'Bugs', 'Chores'. The banners do the job a function boundary should. Preferred fix is per-section builder helpers whose names replace the banners; deleting the banners alone is acceptable.
- 96 '# ---...---' divider lines (48 blocks) across 14 test files, each sitting directly on top of the class it names — '# Unit tests for validate_issue' above 'class TestValidateIssue:' whose docstring already says 'Test individual issue record validation'. Three restatements of one fact. Heaviest: tests/test_validate.py (18 lines), tests/test_cmd_graph.py (16, inside a class body), tests/test_merge_driver.py (12), tests/test_cli_helpers.py (10), tests/test_git_commands.py (8), tests/test_manual_conflict_recovery.py (6).
- src/dogcat/models.py:655 and :657 — two rule lines bracketing '# Backward-compatible re-exports'. Delete the rules only; the PEP 562 paragraph below earns its place.

Ordinal and section labels with no code anchor:
- src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py:156, 171, 186, 199, 217 — '# Check 1:' through '# Check 5:' duplicate the HealthCheck description= string three to eight lines below, and inserting a check means hand-renumbering with nothing failing if you do not.
- src/dogcat/cli/_validate.py:167, 177, 187, 198, 377, 389 — '# Required fields', '# Status validation', '# Issue type validation', '# Priority validation' restate the constant names beneath them.
- src/dogcat/cli/_validate.py:476, src/dogcat/constants.py:20, src/dogcat/config.py:32, src/dogcat/storage.py:525, src/dogcat/inbox.py:213 — lone section markers echoing the names that follow.
- src/dogcat/storage.py:1076-1125 — seven block labels ('# Collect issues to rename' ... '# Cascade to links') paraphrasing the loop beneath. If the collision pre-check must run before any mutation, keep that one and say why (a partial rename leaves a half-renamed store).

Comments and docstrings restating the code:
- src/dogcat/idgen.py:313, 317, 325; src/dogcat/tui/dashboard.py:202, 229, 251, 384, 408, 418, 512; src/dogcat/storage.py:231, 236; src/dogcat/inbox.py:73; src/dogcat/models.py:243; src/dogcat/deps.py:49, 120, 158, 221, 245 ('storage: The storage instance' five times).
- src/dogcat/web/propose/routes.py:60 — _is_valid_namespace copies the first line of constants.is_valid_namespace's docstring while dropping the part that mattered: the ASCII whitelist, the 1-64 cap, and the NFKC-before-calling contract. Replace with why the alias exists plus a pointer to the canonical.

Constraint: pyproject.toml enables ruff's full D family, so a public docstring cannot be deleted. For docstring rows replace the echo with the missing constraint — models.py's enum one-liners should say that UNKNOWN is a forward-compat sentinel and that a tombstone is not 'closed'; storage.py:1689/1694 should say all_dependencies/all_links return a copy; config.py:173/185 should say whether the returned path exists. models.py:593 (LinkType) is the counter-example done right — copy its shape.

MUST NOT be touched: idgen.py's '36**2 = 1296x keyspace' and 'Last resort' notes; models.py's PEP 562 paragraph; dashboard.py's '# Narrow mode: push modal editor' and the 'recompose() is async' comment; storage.py's _bad_lines and memoization comments; deps.py's detect_cycles RecursionError note and _BLOCKING_STATUSES rationale; constants.py's DEFAULT_NAMESPACE, SPLIT_PANE_MIN_*, GITATTRIBUTES_ENTRY, STATUS_VALUES_HELP and MAX_PRIME_TOKENS comments; storage.py's mixin-provenance comment (delete only the '# Event emission helpers' label above it).

Also in scope, from the llm-slop lens: src/dogcat/storage.py:191 has a stray leading comma from a bad rewrap ('# , so ID-targeted commands don't construct the whole') — rewrap those three lines.
acceptance: Every listed divider, ordinal and restating comment is gone or replaced with the missing fact. Every protected comment listed above survives verbatim. just lint-all and just test-all pass.

title: Delete decorative dividers, ordinal labels and code-restating comments repo-wide
Merge-driver prose claims git falls back to its default merge on exit 1 — it does not
description:
Three sites say the merge driver exits 1 'so git falls back to its default merge strategy'. That is false. Git treats a non-zero merge-driver exit as a conflict on that path: it leaves the ours-side file (%A) exactly as it was and marks the path conflicted. No fallback merge runs. AGENTS.md already documents the real behaviour ('the file holds ours-side content only — staging it discards the other branch's issues'), so the source contradicts the repo's own guardrail doc.

Cost: the log message at _cmd_docs.py:481 is what a user sees at the exact moment the driver fails. It reassures them that git handled it, so they stage the file and silently drop every issue from the other branch.

Sites:
- src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py:444 — command docstring
- src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py:481 — user-facing log line
- tests/test_merge_driver.py:766 — test docstring ('exits 1 so git falls back'), which is what a maintainer reads when deciding the exit code is safe
acceptance: All three sites state that git marks the path conflicted and keeps ours-side content. The word 'falls back' appears at none of them. The log line warns against staging the file blindly. No behaviour change: the driver still exits 1.
closed_reason: Merge-driver prose now states git marks the path conflicted

title: Merge-driver prose claims git falls back to its default merge on exit 1 — it does not
Document why InboxStorage._append has no should_compact check — copying the sibling would erase the inbox event log
description:
JSONLStorage._append runs a should_compact() check that can trigger a full rewrite. InboxStorage._append does not, and that omission is load-bearing: InboxStorage._save_locked serializes only proposal records, so any rewrite of inbox.jsonl drops every event record the shared emitter appended. JSONLStorage._save_locked preserves events via compact_snapshot, so the parallel class names read as an accidental inconsistency rather than a deliberate divergence.

Cost: a maintainer restoring parity between the two _append methods destroys inbox history, and nothing in the file warns them. The fact currently lives only in docs/web-ui.md, which nobody reads while editing inbox.py.

Sites:
- src/dogcat/inbox.py:189 (_append) — needs the do-not-add-compaction warning
- src/dogcat/inbox.py:166/171 (_save / _save_locked) — needs the proposals-only rewrite statement and the explicit contrast with JSONLStorage._save_locked
acceptance: inbox.py states at both sites that the rewrite is proposals-only, that it therefore drops event records, that this diverges from JSONLStorage._save_locked on purpose, and that _append must not gain a should_compact branch. No behaviour change.
closed_reason: inbox.py documents the proposals-only rewrite and the compaction ban

title: Document why InboxStorage._append has no should_compact check — copying the sibling would erase the inbox event log
strip_control_chars docstring claims a guarantee the close/delete paths do not honour
description:
src/dogcat/models.py:509 says the helper is 'used by validate_issue/validate_proposal so the storage layer can never persist a record carrying \x1b[2J'. The strip runs on the create() and update() paths only. JSONLStorage.close() (storage.py:1147) and delete() (storage.py:1255) assign closed_reason / deleted_reason and append the record with no validate_issue call, so a reason string containing a terminal escape is written verbatim to issues.jsonl. Records arriving via merge or compaction are not re-validated either.

The very next docstring in the file (sanitize_for_terminal) already concedes the hole with 'even if a record predates the validate-time strip', so the two docstrings contradict each other.

Scope note: this issue is the prose fix only. Whether close()/delete() should also strip is a behaviour question — file it separately if wanted.

Site: src/dogcat/models.py:509
acceptance: The docstring names the covered paths (create, update) instead of asserting an absolute, states that close/delete reasons and merge/compaction-arriving records are not re-validated, and directs callers to render through sanitize_for_terminal. No behaviour change in this issue.
closed_reason: strip_control_bytes docstring names its actual coverage

title: strip_control_chars docstring claims a guarantee the close/delete paths do not honour
_resolve_dogcats_path docstring claims parity with the hardened walk-up it does not implement
description:
src/dogcat/config.py:611 — _resolve_dogcats_path walks up from the cwd looking for a .dogcatrc and accepts the first one it finds. Its docstring says it 'mirrors the walk-up logic in cli._helpers.find_dogcats_dir'. It does not. The real walk-up applies get_rc_walkup_boundary and refuse_if_rc_target_cross_user; this copy is unbounded to the filesystem root, applies no cross-user refusal, and swallows a malformed rc with 'except ValueError: pass'. Both sibling walk-ups (_find_rc_parent in this same file, walkup_find_store in cli/_helpers.py) carry explicit rationale for those guards.

Cost: the word 'mirrors' tells a reader the hardening is present. It is not, so a planted /tmp/.dogcatrc can steer namespace resolution through this path without hitting the defense the other path enforces.

Scope note: prose only. If the missing guards are a real defect rather than a deliberate exemption, that is a separate issue — this one just makes the docstring tell the truth.
acceptance: The docstring no longer claims parity. It states that this walk is unbounded and applies no cross-user refusal, unlike _find_rc_parent and walkup_find_store, and either gives the reason it is safe here or says the rationale is unknown. No behaviour change.
closed_reason: _resolve_dogcats_path no longer claims parity with the hardened walk-ups

title: _resolve_dogcats_path docstring claims parity with the hardened walk-up it does not implement
Explain the or-not-and archive filter in storage.py before someone 'fixes' it
description:
src/dogcat/storage.py:1674 and :1680 filter in-memory dependencies and links after an archive rewrite with:

    if dep.issue_id not in archived_ids or dep.depends_on_id not in archived_ids

The 'or' reads like an 'and' typo. It is not: it is the De Morgan inverse of classify_archived_line's rule that an edge is archived only when BOTH endpoints are archived. A half-archived edge stays in issues.jsonl, so it must stay in memory too.

Cost: changing it to 'and' drops in-memory edges whose surviving endpoint is still live, desyncing memory from the file that was just rewritten. Nothing at either call site records the constraint, so the 'fix' looks obviously correct.

Sites: src/dogcat/storage.py:1674, :1680
acceptance: Both sites carry a comment stating that 'or' is deliberate, that it mirrors classify_archived_line's both-endpoints rule, and what breaks if it becomes 'and'. No behaviour change.
closed_reason: Both archive filters explain the deliberate or

title: Explain the or-not-and archive filter in storage.py before someone 'fixes' it
with_ns_shim docstring describes a global-callback mechanism that does not exist
description:
src/dogcat/cli/_helpers.py:43 — the 'why' paragraph on with_ns_shim says the --namespace / --all-namespaces flags are 'owned by the global Typer callback' and that 'the actual filter is applied by get_namespace_filter() reading the process state set by the global callback'.

None of that is true. The global callback in cli/__init__.py declares only --json and -C/--repo. No namespace process state exists. get_namespace_filter() reads config plus an explicit argument. The shim kwargs.pop()s both values and discards them, so 'dcat close ID --namespace ns' parses fine and filters nothing.

What the shim actually buys: the command parses the options without error, and _ns_filter_from_ctx (cli/_completions.py:20) can read them off the Click context during tab completion.

Cost: a reader debugging why --namespace has no effect on a mutation command is sent to a callback that never touches namespaces.
acceptance: The docstring states the real reason the options are declared (parse compatibility plus completion via ctx.params), names _ns_filter_from_ctx as the consumer, and says plainly that the runtime command ignores the values. No behaviour change.
closed_reason: with_ns_shim docstring states parse-compat plus completion, no global state

title: with_ns_shim docstring describes a global-callback mechanism that does not exist
close() docstring tells the reader to run dcat reopen on a tombstone, which reopen rejects
description:
src/dogcat/storage.py:1165 — the close() docstring says a tombstoned issue 'cannot be closed; use dcat reopen first'. reopen() (storage.py:1232) raises ValueError for any status other than CLOSED, so that instruction cannot succeed. close()'s own raised error already says the opposite and correct thing: 'A tombstone is permanent; no command restores it.'

So one method carries two contradictory statements about tombstones, and the wrong one is the one a reader hits first.
acceptance: The 'use dcat reopen first' clause is gone and the docstring states that a tombstone is terminal, matching the error text the method already raises. No behaviour change.
closed_reason: close() docstring states a tombstone is terminal

title: close() docstring tells the reader to run dcat reopen on a tombstone, which reopen rejects
Two hand-rolled atomic writes skip atomic_rewrite_jsonl's mode preservation with no note saying why
description:
_jsonl_io.atomic_rewrite_jsonl documents mode preservation as load-bearing: without it 'a shared .dogcats becomes inaccessible to everyone except the writer after the first compaction'. Two write paths reimplement tempfile-write + replace() inline and omit that step, with no comment recording whether the omission was considered:

- src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py:399 — dcat git rebase
- src/dogcat/cli/_cmd_docs.py:467 — the merge-driver command

Cost: on a shared store (see docs/sharing-a-database.md) either path can leave issues.jsonl readable only by the last writer, and the helper that knows this is one import away.

Scope note: prose only. Routing these through atomic_rewrite_jsonl would be a behaviour change — file it separately if that is the preferred fix.
acceptance: Both sites carry a comment saying they do not use atomic_rewrite_jsonl, what that skips (mode preservation), and either the reason it is safe here or that the reason is unknown.
closed_reason: Both hand-rolled atomic writes note the skipped mode preservation

title: Two hand-rolled atomic writes skip atomic_rewrite_jsonl's mode preservation with no note saying why
merge_jsonl's Returns section omits that unrecognised record types are dropped from the output
description:
src/dogcat/merge_driver.py:519 — the merge_jsonl docstring enumerates the four record kinds it merges but never says what happens to anything else. A record whose classify_record() result is 'unknown' — for example a record_type written by a newer dcat — does not appear in the returned list at all.

Both callers (dcat git merge-driver and dcat git rebase) write the returned list over the file verbatim. So for a caller, 'dropped from the result' means 'erased from the store', and the docstring gives no hint that forward-compat records are at risk.

The assembly order of the returned list (issues, proposals, deps, links, then events sorted by timestamp) is also undocumented even though the list IS the file content.
acceptance: Returns: states that only issue, proposal, event, dependency and link records survive, that any other record_type is dropped, that callers overwriting the file therefore erase it, and documents the assembly order. No behaviour change.

CLI root callback has no docstring for its three process-wide side effects
description:
src/dogcat/cli/__init__.py:21 — the Typer root callback is the entry point for every dcat invocation and has no docstring. The leading underscore exempts it from ruff's D103, so lint never asked for one.

Three undocumented behaviours, all process-wide:
1. -C/--repo resolves the path strictly and calls os.chdir() on the process before any subcommand runs, exiting 1 if the path is missing or not a directory.
2. --json resets and sets module-global JSON state that every command reads via is_json().
3. A bare 'dcat' with no subcommand prints help and exits 0.

Cost: anyone adding a command or writing a test against the CLI has to read the body to learn that the process cwd moves under them.
acceptance: The callback carries a docstring covering all three behaviours, naming os.chdir() and the global JSON state explicitly. No behaviour change.
closed_reason: Root callback documents chdir, global JSON state and bare-dcat help

description:
src/dogcat/models.py:414 — the UpdateRequest docstring says 'Field names mirror JSONLStorage.UPDATABLE_FIELDS'. UpdateRequest has 17 fields; UPDATABLE_FIELDS has 24. The seven absent ones are closed_at, closed_by, deleted_at, deleted_by, deleted_reason, original_type and comments.

Five file:line citations in docs and tests point at the wrong lines
description:
Line-number citations in prose rot on the first edit above the cited line. Five are already wrong, and three reviewer lenses caught them independently:

- docs/web-ui.md:25 — cites constants.py:291 for the CSP string; WEB_CSP_HEADER is at constants.py:305, and 291 lands inside an unrelated declaration.
- docs/cli-conventions.md:17 — cites _cmd_config.py:39 for _KNOWN_KEYS; it is at :42, and 39 is the closing brace of _ARRAY_KEYS, so a reader edits the wrong constant.
- docs/cli-conventions.md:50 — cites _cmd_chart.py:146 for _complete_by_values; defined at :150.
- docs/merge-coverage.md:28 — cites merge_driver.py:309-318 for _ISSUE_STATUS_RANK; the dict spans 311-320, so the cited range starts mid-comment and cuts off 'tombstone' — the highest rank, which is exactly what that row's finality argument rests on.
- tests/test_merge_driver.py:352 — same wrong 309-318 range.

Preferred fix is to drop the numbers entirely and cite the symbol name, which is grep-able and cannot rot. Note that four further citations elsewhere in these docs are currently correct; converting all of them to symbol names in the same pass stops the whole class of finding recurring.
acceptance: No wrong line citation remains. Either the five ranges are corrected or, preferably, the file:line form is replaced by symbol names throughout the docs set.
